bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第208卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 208.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 208.

sentences.zh: 卷第二百八

translations.literal: Volume 208.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 208.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十四】 起旃蒙大荒落二月，盡強圉協洽，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 24] From Zhanmeng Dahuangluo, second month, through Qiangyu Xiehe; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 24] From Zhanmeng Dahuangluo, second month, through Qiangyu Xiehe—a little more than two years in all.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛亥，帝帥百官詣上陽宮問太后起居；

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinhai, the emperor led the hundred officials to the Shangyang Palace to inquire after the empress dowager's health;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinhai, the emperor led the entire court to the Shangyang Palace to inquire after the Empress Dowager's health;

sentences.zh: 自是每十日一往。

translations.literal: from this time he went once every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter he went once every ten days.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，復國號曰唐。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, the dynastic name was restored to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the dynasty's name was restored to Tang.

sentences.zh: 郊廟、社稷、陵寢、百官、旗幟、服色、文字皆如永淳以前故事。

translations.literal: Suburban and temple sacrifices, the altars of soil and grain, imperial tombs, the hundred offices, banners and flags, dress colors, and script were all as in the precedents before Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple rites, the altars of soil and grain, imperial tombs, official ranks, banners, dress codes, and script all reverted to the pre-Yongchun conventions.

sentences.zh: 復以神都為東都，北都為-{并}-州，老君為玄元皇帝。

translations.literal: Shendu was again made the eastern capital, the northern capital again named Bingzhou, and Lord Lao again titled Emperor Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Capital was again designated the Eastern Capital, the Northern Capital again governed as Bingzhou, and Lord Lao was again honored as Emperor Xuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，鳳閣侍郎、同平章事韋承慶貶高要尉；

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Fengge Shilang and Associate Director of the Chancellery Wei Chengqing was demoted to commandant of Gaoyao;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Director of the Chancellery Wei Chengqing was demoted to commandant of Gaoyao;

sentences.zh: 正諫大夫、同平章事房融除名，流高州；

translations.literal: Corrective Reminder Grandee and Associate Director of the Chancellery Fang Rong was struck from the rolls and banished to Gaozhou;
translations.idiomatic: Corrective Reminder Grandee and Associate Director of the Chancellery Fang Rong was struck from the rolls and exiled to Gaozhou;

sentences.zh: 司禮卿崔神慶流欽州。

translations.literal: Director of Court Ceremonies Cui Shenqing was banished to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Court Ceremonies Cui Shenqing was exiled to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊再思為戶部尚書、同中書門下三品、西京留守。

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi was made Minister of Revenue, Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin, and defender of the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi was appointed Minister of Revenue, Grand Councilor of the Second Rank, and defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 太后之遷上陽宮也，太僕卿、同中書門下三品姚元之獨嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager was moved to the Shangyang Palace, Grand Master of the Stud and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin Yao Yuanzhi alone sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager was moved to the Shangyang Palace, Grand Master of the Stud and Grand Councilor Yao Yuanzhi alone sobbed aloud.

sentences.zh: 桓彥范、張柬之謂曰：「今日豈公涕泣時邪！

translations.literal: Huan Yuanfan and Zhang Jianzhi said to him, "Is today the time for you to weep!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yuanfan and Zhang Jianzhi said to him, "Is this the day for you to weep?

sentences.zh: 恐公禍由此始。」

translations.literal: I fear your disaster will begin from this."
translations.idiomatic: I fear your ruin will begin here."

sentences.zh: 元之曰：「元之事則天皇帝久，乍此辭違，悲不能忍。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi said, "Yuan served the Zetian Emperor long; suddenly to part thus, grief cannot be borne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi said, "I served the Zetian Emperor for many years; to part from her so abruptly, I cannot bear the grief.

sentences.zh: 且元之前日從公誅奸逆，人臣之義也；

translations.literal: Moreover, when Yuan the other day followed you in executing treacherous rebels, that was a minister's duty;
translations.idiomatic: And when I followed you the other day in executing traitors, that was a minister's duty;

sentences.zh: 今日別舊君，亦人臣之義也，雖獲罪，實所甘心。」

translations.literal: today to take leave of an old sovereign is also a minister's duty; though I incur punishment, I am truly content."
translations.idiomatic: today to bid farewell to my former sovereign is also a minister's duty; though I be punished for it, I accept that willingly."

sentences.zh: 是日，出為亳州刺史。

translations.literal: That day he was sent out as prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was posted out as prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，立妃韋氏為皇后，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Consort Wei was established as empress, and the empire was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Consort Wei was made empress and the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 追贈後父玄貞為上洛王、母崔氏為妃。

translations.literal: Posthumously the empress's father Xuanzhen was enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo and her mother, the Lady Cui, as consort.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's late father Xuanzhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo and her mother, Lady Cui, as a consort.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺賈虛己上疏，以為：「異姓不王，古今通制。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Jia Xuji submitted a memorial, holding that "men of other surnames are not enfeoffed as kings—this is the universal rule through antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Jia Xuji submitted a memorial arguing that "enfeoffing men of other surnames as kings has never been permitted in any age.

sentences.zh: 今中興之始，萬姓喁喁以觀陛下之政；

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of restoration, the myriad people murmur to observe Your Majesty's governance;
translations.idiomatic: At the dawn of restoration, the people are watching Your Majesty's every act;

sentences.zh: 而先王后族，非所以廣德美於天下也。

translations.literal: yet to ennoble the empress's clan first is not the way to spread virtue and beauty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: yet to ennoble the empress's kin first is no way to spread virtue throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 且先朝贈后父太原王，殷鑒不遠，須防其漸。

translations.literal: Moreover, the previous court enfeoffed the empress's father as Prince of Taiyuan—the warning is not far off; one must guard against the gradual encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: The previous court enfeoffed an empress's father as Prince of Taiyuan—that lesson is recent; we must guard against the first step on a dangerous path.

sentences.zh: 若以恩制已行，宜令皇后固讓，則益增謙沖之德矣。」

translations.literal: If the favoring decree has already been issued, the empress should be made firmly to decline, and then modesty and restraint will be increased all the more."
translations.idiomatic: If the decree has already gone forth, let the empress firmly decline the honor—that would only enhance her reputation for humility."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 初，韋后生邵王重潤、長寧、安樂二公主，上之遷房陵也，安樂公主生於道中，上特愛之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lady Wei bore Prince Shao Chongrun and the two princesses of Changning and Anle; when the emperor was moved to Fangling, Princess Anle was born on the road, and the emperor loved her especially.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lady Wei had borne Prince Shao Chongrun and the princesses of Changning and Anle. When the emperor was sent to Fangling, Princess Anle was born on the journey, and he cherished her above all.

sentences.zh: 上在房陵與後同幽閉，備嘗艱危，情愛甚篤。

translations.literal: The emperor at Fangling was confined together with the consort, fully tasting hardship and peril; their affection was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: At Fangling the emperor and his consort were confined together, sharing every hardship; their bond ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 上每聞敕使至，輒惶恐欲自殺，后止之曰：「禍福無常，寧失一死，何遽如是！」

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor heard that an imperial messenger had arrived, he would panic and wish to kill himself; the consort stopped him, saying, "Fortune and misfortune are inconstant—better to miss one death than to be so hasty!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever word came that an imperial messenger was approaching, the emperor would panic and try to take his own life. The consort would stop him, saying, "Fortune and misfortune are unpredictable—would you throw away your one life so rashly?"

sentences.zh: 上嘗與后私誓曰：「異時幸復見天日，當惟卿所欲，不相禁御。」

translations.literal: The emperor once privately swore to the consort, "If by good fortune we again see the light of day, I shall grant whatever you desire and not restrain you."
translations.idiomatic: Once he swore to her in private, "If we ever see the light of day again, you may have whatever you wish—I shall not hold you back."

sentences.zh: 及再為皇后，遂干預朝政，如武後在高宗之世。

translations.literal: When she again became empress, she thereupon intervened in court politics, as Empress Wu had in the time of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: When she again became empress, she intervened in state affairs just as Empress Wu had under Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 桓彥范上表，以為：「《易》稱『無攸遂，在中饋，貞吉』，《書》稱『牝雞之辰，惟家之索』，伏見陛下每臨朝，皇后必施帷幔坐殿上，預聞政事。

translations.literal: Huan Yuanfan submitted a memorial, holding that "the Changes says, 'Do not pursue affairs; remain in charge of the inner provision—steadfastness brings good fortune,' and the Documents says, 'When the hen crows at dawn, the household is undone.' I observe that whenever Your Majesty holds court, the empress always hangs a curtain and sits in the hall, hearing affairs of government in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yuanfan submitted a memorial arguing that "the Book of Changes says a woman should not pursue public affairs but keep to the inner household, and the Book of Documents warns that when the hen crows at dawn, the family is ruined. I observe that whenever Your Majesty holds court, the empress sits behind a curtain on the dais and hears state business in advance.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀自古帝王，未有與婦人共政而不破國亡身者也。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed that from antiquity to the present no emperor who shared government with a woman has failed to lose his state and his life.
translations.idiomatic: In all history, no ruler who shared power with a woman has escaped ruin of state and person alike.

sentences.zh: 且以陰乘陽，違天也；

translations.literal: Moreover, for yin to ride upon yang violates Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: For yin to dominate yang is to defy Heaven;

sentences.zh: 以婦陵夫，違人也。

translations.literal: for a woman to tower over her husband violates humanity.
translations.idiomatic: for a wife to tower over her husband is to defy human order.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下覽古今之戒，以社稷蒼生為念，令皇后專居中宮，治陰教，勿出外朝干國政。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to review the warnings of past and present, take thought for the altars of state and the black-haired people, and order the empress to remain solely in the inner palace, governing feminine instruction, and not to come out to the outer court and meddle in national affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed the lessons of history, keep the realm and its people in mind, and confine the empress to the inner palace to govern women's affairs, not to the outer court and the business of state."

sentences.zh: 先是，胡僧慧范以妖妄游權貴之門，與張易之兄弟善，韋後亦重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the barbarian monk Huifan, by sorcery and delusion, frequented the gates of the powerful; he was on good terms with Zhang Yizhi and his brothers, and Empress Wei also esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the foreign monk Huifan had traded on sorcery and delusion to move among the powerful; he was close to Zhang Yizhi and his brothers, and Empress Wei also favored him.

sentences.zh: 及易之誅，復稱慧范預其謀，以功加銀青光祿大夫，賜爵上庸縣公，出入宮掖，上數微行幸其捨。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, it was again claimed that Huifan had taken part in the plot; for this merit he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Shangyong County, and admitted to the inner palace; the emperor several times went in disguise to visit his lodge.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhi's execution, Huifan was said to have shared in the plot against him; rewarded with the rank of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and the title Duke of Shangyong, he came and went within the palace precincts, and the emperor often slipped out in disguise to visit his quarters.

sentences.zh: 彥范復表言慧范執左道以亂政，請誅之。

translations.literal: Yuanfan again memorialized that Huifan practiced heterodox ways to disorder government and asked that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan memorialized again that Huifan practiced heterodox arts to corrupt government and begged that he be put to death.

sentences.zh: 上皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 初，武後誅唐宗室，有才德者先死，惟吳王恪之子鬱林侯千里褊躁無才，又數獻符瑞，故獨得免。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Wu executed the Tang imperial clan, those with talent and virtue died first; only the son of Prince Wu of Wu, the Marquis of Yulin Qianli, being narrow, impetuous, and without talent, and repeatedly presenting omens and portents, alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu purged the Tang imperial house, the talented and virtuous were killed first. Only Qianli, son of Prince Wu of Wu and Marquis of Yulin, survived—he was narrow-minded, impetuous, and talentless, and kept presenting bogus portents.

sentences.zh: 上即位，立為成王，拜左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he was established as Prince of Cheng and appointed Left Commander-in-Chief of the Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he was made Prince of Cheng and appointed Left Commander-in-Chief of the Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 武後所誅唐諸王、妃、主、駙馬等，皆無人葬埋，子孫或流竄嶺表，或拘囚歷年，或逃匿民間，為人傭保。

translations.literal: The Tang princes, consorts, princesses, imperial sons-in-law, and others whom Empress Wu had executed had none to bury them; their descendants were either exiled beyond the ranges, or imprisoned for years, or hid among the people as hired laborers.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang princes, consorts, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law whom Empress Wu had killed lay unburied; their descendants were exiled beyond the mountains, imprisoned for years, or hidden among common folk as hired hands.

sentences.zh: 至是，制州縣求訪其柩，以禮改葬，追復官爵，召其子孫，使之承襲，無子孫者為擇後置之。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to seek out their coffins, reinter them with proper rites, restore their offices and titles posthumously, summon their descendants, and have them inherit; where there were no descendants, successors were chosen and installed.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the provinces to find their remains, reinter them with proper rites, restore their offices and titles, summon their descendants to inherit, and where none survived, appoint successors.

sentences.zh: 既而宗室子孫相繼而至，皆召見，涕泣舞蹈，各以親疏襲爵拜官有差。

translations.literal: Before long the imperial clansmen's descendants arrived one after another; all were summoned to audience, weeping and performing the dance of obeisance; each according to degree of kinship inherited titles and received offices with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Soon imperial descendants arrived in succession; all were received in audience, weeping and performing the ritual dance; each was given rank and office according to the closeness of his kinship.

sentences.zh: 二張之誅也，洛州長史薛季昶謂張柬之、敬暉曰：「二凶雖除，產、祿猶在，去草不去根，終當復生。」

translations.literal: At the execution of the two Zhangs, Luozhou Chief Administrator Xue Jichang said to Zhang Jianzhi and Jing Hui, "Though the two villains are removed, Chan and Lu still remain; to remove grass without removing the root—they will surely grow again."
translations.idiomatic: When the two Zhangs were executed, Luozhou Chief Administrator Xue Jichang told Zhang Jianzhi and Jing Hui, "The two villains are gone, but Chan and Lu still live. Pull grass without taking the root and it will grow back."

sentences.zh: 二人曰：「大事已定，彼猶機上肉耳，夫何能為！

translations.literal: The two men said, "The great affair is already settled; they are but meat on the chopping block—what can they do!
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "The great matter is settled; they are meat on the block—what can they do?

sentences.zh: 所誅已多，不可復益也。」

translations.literal: Those executed are already many; we cannot add more."
translations.idiomatic: Enough blood has been shed; we cannot add to it."

sentences.zh: 季昶歎曰：「吾不知死所矣！」

translations.literal: Jichang sighed, "I do not know where I shall die!"
translations.idiomatic: Jichang sighed, "I no longer know where I shall meet my end!"

sentences.zh: 朝邑尉武強劉幽求亦謂桓彥范、敬暉曰：「武三思尚存，公輩終無葬地；

translations.literal: Chaoyi Commandant of Wuqiang Liu Youqiu also said to Huan Yuanfan and Jing Hui, "While Wu Sansi still lives, you gentlemen in the end will have no place of burial;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi Commandant Liu Youqiu of Wuqiang also told Huan Yuanfan and Jing Hui, "While Wu Sansi lives, you will never have a grave to lie in;

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，噬臍無及。」

translations.literal: if you do not plan early, to bite your navel will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: if you do not act soon, you will bite your navel in vain."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: They did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen.

sentences.zh: 上女安樂公主適三思子崇訓。

translations.literal: The emperor's daughter Princess Anle was married to Sansi's son Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's daughter, Princess Anle, was married to Sansi's son Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 上官婉兒者，儀之女孫也，儀死，沒入掖庭，辯慧善屬文，明習吏事。

translations.literal: Shangguan Wan'er was the granddaughter of Yi; when Yi died she was sent into the palace women's quarters; she was eloquent and clever and skilled in composition, and thoroughly versed in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Wan'er was the granddaughter of Shangguan Yi. After Yi's death she was sent to the palace women's quarters; she was eloquent, clever with words, and thoroughly versed in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 則天愛之，自聖歷以後，百司表奏多令參決；

translations.literal: Zetian favored her; from the Shengli era onward, many memorials and reports of the hundred offices were ordered decided with her participation;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian favored her; from the Shengli era onward, many official memorials were referred to her for decision;

sentences.zh: 及上即位，又使專掌制命，益委任之，拜為婕妤，用事於中。

translations.literal: when the emperor took the throne, he again had her exclusively manage edicts, entrusted her all the more, appointed her Lady of Handsome Fairness, and she wielded power within.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor took the throne, he put her in charge of edicts, trusted her still more, made her a Lady of Handsome Fairness, and she wielded power within the palace.

sentences.zh: 三思通焉，故黨於武氏，又薦三思於韋後，引入禁中，上遂與三思圖議政事，張柬之等皆受制於三思矣。

translations.literal: Sansi had relations with her; therefore she sided with the Wu clan, and also recommended Sansi to Empress Wei and brought him into the forbidden precincts; the emperor thereupon deliberated on government with Sansi, and Zhang Jianzhi and the others all came under Sansi's control.
translations.idiomatic: She had an affair with Sansi, sided with the Wu clan, and recommended Sansi to Empress Wei, bringing him into the inner palace. The emperor then discussed state affairs with Sansi, and Zhang Jianzhi and his fellows all fell under Sansi's sway.

sentences.zh: 上使韋後與三思雙陸，而自居旁為之點籌；

translations.literal: The emperor had Empress Wei and Sansi play double-six, while he himself sat to the side and counted the stakes for them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Empress Wei and Sansi play backgammon while he sat beside them and kept score;

sentences.zh: 三思遂與後通，由是武氏之勢復振。

translations.literal: Sansi thereupon had relations with the empress, and thereby the Wu clan's power revived.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi then took the empress as his lover, and the Wu clan's power revived.

sentences.zh: 張柬之等數勸上誅諸武，上不聽。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi and the others repeatedly urged the emperor to execute the various Wus; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi and his allies repeatedly urged the emperor to execute the Wu clan; he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 柬之等曰：「革命之際，宗室諸李，誅夷略盡；

translations.literal: Jianzhi and the others said, "At the time of the revolution, the various Lis of the imperial clan were executed and exterminated almost entirely;
translations.idiomatic: They said, "During the revolution the Li imperial clan was all but wiped out;

sentences.zh: 今賴天地之靈，陛下返正，而武氏濫官僭爵，按堵如故，豈遠近所望邪！

translations.literal: now relying on the spirits of Heaven and Earth, Your Majesty has returned to the true succession, yet the Wu clan holds offices and titles in excess, living at ease as before—is this what near and far hoped for!
translations.idiomatic: now, by Heaven's grace, Your Majesty has restored the true line, yet the Wu still hold inflated offices and titles and live as before—is this what the realm hoped for?

sentences.zh: 願頗抑損其祿位以慰天下！」

translations.literal: We wish that you would somewhat reduce their salaries and ranks to comfort the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to cut back their salaries and ranks to comfort the empire!"

sentences.zh: 又不聽。

translations.literal: Again he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Again he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 柬之等或撫床歎憤，或彈指出血，曰：「主上昔為英王，時稱勇烈，吾所以不誅諸武者，欲使上自誅之，以張天子之威耳。

translations.literal: Jianzhi and the others would stroke the bed and sigh in anger, or flick their fingers until blood came, saying, "Our lord in former days was Prince of Ying, then called brave and fierce; the reason we did not execute the various Wus was to have Your Majesty execute them himself, thereby displaying the Son of Heaven's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: They would beat the bed in fury or flick their fingers until the blood came, saying, "Our lord was once Prince of Ying, famed for courage; we spared the Wu clan so that you might kill them yourself and show the Son of Heaven's authority.

sentences.zh: 今反如此，事勢已去，知復奈何！」

translations.literal: Now it turns out thus—the momentum is already gone; what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Now look at him—the moment is lost. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 上數微服幸武三思第，監察微史清河崔皎密疏諫曰：「國命初復，則天皇帝在西宮，人心猶有附會；

translations.literal: The emperor several times went in disguise to visit Wu Sansi's residence; Supervising Censor Qinghe Cui Jiao submitted a secret memorial remonstrating, saying, "The dynastic mandate has just been restored; the Zetian Emperor is in the western palace, and hearts still have attachments;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often slipped out in disguise to visit Wu Sansi's house. Supervising Censor Cui Jiao of Qinghe submitted a secret memorial: "The dynasty has only just been restored; the Zetian Emperor still sits in the western palace, and many hearts still look to her;

sentences.zh: 周之舊臣，列居朝廷，陛下奈何輕有外游，不察豫且之禍！」

translations.literal: old ministers of Zhou fill the court ranks—how can Your Majesty lightly go abroad and not heed the disaster of Yuxu!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's old ministers still fill the court—how can Your Majesty roam abroad so lightly and not see the trap that caught Yuxu?"

sentences.zh: 上洩之，三思之黨切齒。

translations.literal: The emperor leaked it; Sansi's faction gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaked the memorial; Sansi's faction gnashed their teeth at Jiao.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以太子賓客武三思為司空、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Heir Apparent's Guest Wu Sansi was made Minister of Works and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Heir Apparent's Guest Wu Sansi was appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍譙王重福，上之庶子也；

translations.literal: Left Regular Attendant Prince of Qiao Chongfu was a son of the emperor by a concubine;
translations.idiomatic: Left Regular Attendant Prince of Qiao Chongfu was a son of the emperor by a concubine;

sentences.zh: 其妃，張易之之甥。

translations.literal: his consort was Zhang Yizhi's niece.
translations.idiomatic: his consort was Zhang Yizhi's niece.

sentences.zh: 韋後惡之，譖於上曰：「重潤之死，重福為之也。」

translations.literal: Empress Wei hated him and slandered him to the emperor, saying, "Chongrun's death was Chongfu's doing."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei hated him and told the emperor, "Chongfu was behind Chongrun's death."

sentences.zh: 由是貶濮州員外刺史，又改均州刺史，常令州司防守之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was demoted to supernumerary prefect of Puzhou, then changed to prefect of Junzhou, and the prefectural offices were regularly ordered to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to supernumerary prefect of Puzhou, then transferred to prefect of Junzhou, with orders that the prefectural staff keep him under guard.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以右散騎常侍安定王武攸暨為司徒、定王。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Right Regular Attendant Prince of Anding Wu Youji was made Minister of Education and Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Right Regular Attendant Prince of Anding Wu Youji was made Minister of Education and Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 辛未，相王固讓太尉及知政事，許之；

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the Prince of Xiang firmly declined Grand Preceptor and participation in government; this was granted;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Prince of Xiang firmly declined the post of Grand Preceptor and a role in government; the emperor agreed;

sentences.zh: 又立為皇太弟，相王固辭而止。

translations.literal: he was again established as imperial younger brother heir, but the Prince of Xiang firmly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: he was then named Imperial Younger Brother Heir, but the Prince of Xiang declined again and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以國子祭酒始平祝欽明同中書門下三品，黃門侍郎、知侍中事韋安石為刑部尚書，罷知政事。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, National University Chancellor of Shiping Zhu Qinming was made Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin; Yellow Gate Vice Minister and Acting Palace Attendant Wei Anshi was made Minister of Justice and ceased participation in government.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, National University Chancellor Zhu Qinming of Shiping was made Grand Councilor; Yellow Gate Vice Minister and Acting Palace Attendant Wei Anshi was made Minister of Justice and removed from the council.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，武三思、武攸暨固辭新官爵及政事，許之，並加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Wu Sansi and Wu Youji firmly declined their new offices, titles, and participation in government; this was granted, and both were additionally given the honorific Kaifu Yitong San Si.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Wu Sansi and Wu Youji declined their new offices and council seats; the emperor agreed and instead gave both the honorific rank of Kaifu Yitong San Si.

sentences.zh: 立皇子義興王重俊為衛王，北海王重茂為溫王，仍以重俊為洛州牧。

translations.literal: The emperor's son Prince of Yixing Chongjun was established as Prince of Wei, Prince of Beihai Chongmao as Prince of Wen, and Chongjun was again made prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yixing Chongjun was made Prince of Wei, Prince of Beihai Chongmao was made Prince of Wen, and Chongjun was also appointed prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲申，制：「文明已來破家子孫皆復舊資廕，唯徐敬業、裴炎不在免限。」

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiashen, an edict stated: "From the Wenming era onward, descendants of ruined families all have their former inherited privileges restored, except Xu Jingye and Pei Yan, who are not within the scope of exemption."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiashen, an edict declared: "From the Wenming era onward, descendants of ruined families shall have their hereditary privileges restored, except for the lines of Xu Jingye and Pei Yan."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，制：「酷吏周興、來俊臣等，已死者追奪官爵，存者皆流嶺南惡地。」

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, an edict stated: "The cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others—those already dead are posthumously stripped of office and title; those still living are all banished to the foul lands south of the ranges."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, an edict declared: "The cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their like—those dead are posthumously stripped of rank; those living are exiled to the foul lands south of the mountains."

sentences.zh: 己丑，以袁恕己為中書令。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Yuan Shuji was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Yuan Shuji was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以安車征安平王武攸緒於嵩山，既至，除太子賓客；

translations.literal: With a comfort carriage Prince of Anping Wu Youxu was summoned from Mount Song; when he arrived, he was made Heir Apparent's Guest;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anping Wu Youxu was summoned from Mount Song in a comfort carriage; on arrival he was made Heir Apparent's Guest;

sentences.zh: 固請還山，許之。

translations.literal: he firmly asked to return to the mountain, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: he asked firmly to return to the mountain, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 制：「梟氏、蟒氏皆復舊姓。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The Xiao clan and the Mang clan are both restored to their former surnames."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The Xiao and Mang clans are restored to their former surnames."

sentences.zh: 術士鄭普思、尚衣奉御葉靜能皆以妖妄為上所信重，夏，四月，墨敕以普思為秘書監，靜能為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The technicians Zheng Pusi and Director of Palace Attire Ye Jingneng were both believed and esteemed by the emperor for sorcery and delusion; in summer, the fourth month, by vermilion rescript Pusi was made Director of the Secretariat and Jingneng National University Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerers Zheng Pusi and Director of Palace Attire Ye Jingneng won the emperor's trust through occult arts. In summer, the fourth month, by vermilion rescript Pusi was made Director of the Secretariat and Jingneng National University Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 桓彥范、崔玄□固執不可，上曰：「已用之，無容遽改。」

translations.literal: Huan Yuanfan and Cui Xuanwei firmly held that this could not be; the emperor said, "They have already been appointed; there is no room for sudden change."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yuanfan and Cui Xuanwei objected firmly, but the emperor said, "The appointments are already made; they cannot be reversed so quickly.

sentences.zh: 彥范曰：「陛下初即位，下制云：『政令皆依貞觀故事。』

translations.literal: Yuanfan said, "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you issued an edict saying, 'Government orders all follow the precedents of the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan said, "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you decreed that all government should follow Zhenguan precedent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，魏徵、虞世南、顏師古為秘書監，孔穎達為國子祭酒，豈普思、靜能之比乎！」

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yan Shigu were Directors of the Secretariat, and Kong Yingda was National University Chancellor—how can Pusi and Jingneng be compared to them!"
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan, Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yan Shigu were Directors of the Secretariat, and Kong Yingda was National University Chancellor—are Pusi and Jingneng fit to stand beside them?

sentences.zh: 庚戌，左拾遺李邕上疏，以為：「《詩》三百，一言以蔽之，曰『思無邪』。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Left Reminder Li Yong submitted a memorial, holding that "the three hundred pieces of the Odes may be covered in one phrase: 'Think without depravity.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Left Reminder Li Yong submitted a memorial arguing that "the three hundred Odes may be summed in one phrase: Think without depravity.

sentences.zh: 若有神仙能令人不死，則秦始皇、漢武帝得之矣；

translations.literal: If there were immortals who could keep men from dying, then Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han would have obtained them;
translations.idiomatic: If immortals could grant eternal life, Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han would have found them;

sentences.zh: 佛能為人福利，則梁武帝得之矣。

translations.literal: if the Buddha could bring men benefit and blessing, then Emperor Wu of Liang would have obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: if the Buddha could bestow blessing on men, Emperor Wu of Liang would have possessed it.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜所以為帝王首者，亦修人事而已。

translations.literal: The reason Yao and Shun stand first among emperors is also simply that they cultivated human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun stand first among rulers because they cultivated human affairs and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 尊寵此屬，何補於國！」

translations.literal: To honor and favor men of this sort—what good does it do the state!"
translations.idiomatic: To honor men of this sort does nothing for the state!

sentences.zh: 上皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 上即位之日，驛召魏元忠於高要；

translations.literal: On the day the emperor took the throne, by express post he summoned Wei Yuanzhong from Gaoyao;
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took the throne, the emperor summoned Wei Yuanzhong from Gaoyao by express post;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至都，拜衛尉卿、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, he reached the capital and was appointed Commandant of the Guard and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he reached the capital and was appointed Commandant of the Guard and Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以魏元忠為兵部尚書，韋安石為吏部尚書，李懷遠為右散騎常侍，唐休璟為輔國大將軍，崔玄□檢校益府長史，楊再思檢校楊府長史，祝欽明為刑部尚書，並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Wei Yuanzhong was made Minister of War, Wei Anshi Minister of Personnel, Li Huaiyuan Right Regular Attendant, Tang Xiujing Grand General Who Supports the State, Cui Xuanwei Acting Chief Administrator of Yizhou Prefecture, Yang Zaisi Acting Chief Administrator of Yangzhou Prefecture, and Zhu Qinming Minister of Justice—all as Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wei Yuanzhong was appointed Minister of War, Wei Anshi Minister of Personnel, Li Huaiyuan Right Regular Attendant, Tang Xiujing Grand General Who Supports the State, Cui Xuanwei Acting Chief Administrator of Yizhou, Yang Zaisi Acting Chief Administrator of Yangzhou, and Zhu Qinming Minister of Justice—all as Grand Councilors of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 元忠等皆以東宮舊僚褒之也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong and the others were all rewarded because they were former staff of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong and the others were all rewarded as former retainers of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以張柬之為中書令。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Zhang Jianzhi was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Zhang Jianzhi was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，追贈故邵王重潤為懿德太子。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the late Prince Shao Chongrun was posthumously enfeoffed as Crown Prince Yide.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the late Prince Shao Chongrun was posthumously honored as Crown Prince Yide.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，遷周廟七主於西京崇尊廟。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day renwu, the seven Zhou temple sovereigns were moved to the Chongzun Temple in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu, the seven Zhou temple sovereigns were moved to the Chongzun Temple in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 制：「武氏三代諱，奏事者皆不得犯。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The taboo names of three generations of the Wu clan—none who submit memorials may violate them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The taboo names of the Wu clan for three generations may not be violated by anyone submitting memorials.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，立太廟、社稷於東都。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain were established in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain were established in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以張柬之等及武攸暨、武三思、鄭普思等十六人皆為立功之人，賜以鐵券，自非反逆，各恕十死。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi and others, together with Wu Youji, Wu Sansi, Zheng Pusi, and sixteen men in all, were all deemed men who had achieved merit; they were granted iron certificates, and unless guilty of rebellion, each was pardoned ten deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi and others, together with Wu Youji, Wu Sansi, Zheng Pusi, and sixteen men in all, were counted as meritorious servants; they were granted iron certificates, and unless guilty of treason, each was pardoned ten capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，敬暉等帥百官上表，以為：「五運迭興，事不兩大。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Jing Hui and others led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial, holding that: "The Five Phases rise in succession; two great powers cannot stand together.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Jing Hui and others led the officials in a memorial arguing: "The Five Phases rise in turn; two supreme powers cannot coexist.

sentences.zh: 天授革命之際，宗室誅竄殆盡，豈得與諸武並封！

translations.literal: At the time of the Tianshou revolution, the imperial clan was executed and banished almost to extinction—how can they be enfeoffed alongside the various Wus!
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianshou revolution, the imperial clan was slaughtered and driven out almost to extinction—how can they be enfeoffed on equal terms with the Wu princes!

sentences.zh: 今天命惟新，而諸武封建如舊，並居京師，開闢以來未有斯理。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's mandate is renewed, yet the various Wus are enfeoffed as before, all dwelling in the capital—since the founding of the realm there has never been such a principle.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven's mandate is renewed, yet the Wu princes remain enfeoffed as before, all dwelling in the capital—since the realm was founded there has never been such a thing.

sentences.zh: 願陛下為社稷計，順遐邇心，降其王爵，以安內外。」

translations.literal: We beg Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, to follow the hearts of men near and far, reduce their princely ranks, and settle inner and outer alike."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, to heed the hearts of men near and far, reduce their princely ranks, and bring peace within and without.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等畏武三思之讒，以考功員外郎崔湜為耳目，伺其動靜。

translations.literal: Jing Hui and others feared Wu Sansi's slander and used Evaluation-of-Merit Vice Director Cui Shi as their eyes and ears to watch his movements.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui and others feared slander from Wu Sansi and used Evaluation-of-Merit Vice Director Cui Shi as their spy to watch his movements.

sentences.zh: 湜見上親三思而忌暉等，乃悉以暉等謀告三思，反為三思用；

translations.literal: Shi saw that the emperor favored Sansi and was wary of Jing Hui and the others; he then reported all of Jing Hui and the others' plans to Sansi and in turn was used by Sansi;
translations.idiomatic: Shi saw that the emperor favored Sansi and distrusted Jing Hui and the others; he then told Sansi everything Jing Hui and the others were planning and was turned to Sansi's use;

sentences.zh: 三思引為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Sansi brought him in as Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi appointed him Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 湜，仁師之孫也。

translations.literal: Shi was the grandson of Renshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the grandson of Cui Renshi.

sentences.zh: 先是，殿中侍御史南皮鄭愔諂事二張，二張敗，貶宣州司士參軍，坐贓，亡入東都，私謁武三思。

translations.literal: Earlier, Palace Disciplinarian Zheng Yin of Nanpi had flattered the Two Zhangs; when the Two Zhangs fell, he was demoted to Military Administrator of Xuanzhou; convicted of embezzlement, he fled into the Eastern Capital and privately called on Wu Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Disciplinarian Zheng Yin of Nanpi had flattered the Two Zhangs; when they fell, he was demoted to Military Administrator of Xuanzhou; convicted of embezzlement, he fled to the Eastern Capital and privately visited Wu Sansi.

sentences.zh: 初見三思，哭甚哀，既而大笑。

translations.literal: When he first saw Sansi, he wept very bitterly; then he laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: When he first met Sansi, he wept bitterly; then he burst into loud laughter.

sentences.zh: 三思素貴重，甚怪之，愔曰：「始見大王而哭，哀大王將戮死而滅族也。

translations.literal: Sansi had always been honored and esteemed and was greatly puzzled by this; Yin said, "When I first saw Your Highness I wept, grieving that Your Highness would be executed and your clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi, who had always been honored and powerful, was greatly puzzled; Yin said, "When I first saw Your Highness I wept, grieving that you would be executed and your clan wiped out.

sentences.zh: 後乃大笑，喜大王之得愔也。

translations.literal: Afterward I laughed, rejoicing that Your Highness had gained Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Then I laughed, rejoicing that Your Highness had gained me.

sentences.zh: 大王雖得天子之意，彼五人皆據將相之權，膽略過人，廢太后如反掌。

translations.literal: Though Your Highness has won the emperor's favor, those five men all hold the power of generals and ministers, their courage and stratagem surpass other men, and they deposed the Empress Dowager as easily as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Highness has the emperor's favor, those five men hold the power of generals and ministers, their courage and stratagem surpass other men's, and they deposed the Empress Dowager as easily as turning the hand over.

sentences.zh: 大王自視勢位與太后孰重？

translations.literal: Does Your Highness consider your power and position heavier, or the Empress Dowager's?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Highness consider your power and position the heavier, or the Empress Dowager's?

sentences.zh: 彼五人日夜切齒，欲噬大王之肉，非盡大王之族不足以快其志。

translations.literal: Those five men grind their teeth day and night, wanting to devour Your Highness's flesh; only exterminating Your Highness's clan would suffice to satisfy their will.
translations.idiomatic: Those five men grind their teeth day and night, longing to devour your flesh; only wiping out your entire clan would satisfy them.

sentences.zh: 大王不去此五人，危如朝露，而晏然尚自以為泰山之安，此愔所以為大王寒心。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness does not remove these five men, your peril is like morning dew, yet you remain at ease and still think yourself as secure as Mount Tai—this is why Yin trembles for Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness does not remove these five men, your peril is like morning dew, yet you remain at ease and still think yourself secure as Mount Tai—this is why I tremble for you.

sentences.zh: 三思大悅，與之登樓，問自安之策，引為中書舍人，與崔湜皆為三思謀主。

translations.literal: Sansi was greatly pleased; he went up a tower with him and asked the strategy for securing himself, brought him in as Secretariat Drafting Officer, and both he and Cui Shi became Sansi's chief strategists.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi was greatly pleased; he went up a tower with him to ask how he might secure himself, appointed him Secretariat Drafting Officer, and both he and Cui Shi became Sansi's chief strategists.

sentences.zh: 三思與韋後日夜譖暉等，云「恃功專權，將不利於社稷。」

translations.literal: Sansi and Empress Wei day and night slandered Jing Hui and the others, saying, "Relying on their merit, they monopolize power and will bring harm to the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Sansi and Empress Wei slandered Jing Hui and the others day and night, saying, "They rely on their merit, monopolize power, and will harm the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 上信之。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed them.

sentences.zh: 三思等因為上畫策：「不若封暉等為王，罷其政事，外不失尊寵功臣，內實奪之權。」

translations.literal: Sansi and the others thereupon laid out a plan for the emperor: "It would be better to enfeoff Jing Hui and the others as kings, remove them from government affairs—outwardly not failing to honor meritorious servants, inwardly actually stripping them of power."
translations.idiomatic: Sansi and the others then advised the emperor: "Better to enfeoff Jing Hui and the others as kings and remove them from government—outwardly still honoring meritorious servants, inwardly actually stripping them of power.

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以侍中齊公敬暉為平陽王，譙公桓彥范為扶陽王，中書令漢陽公張柬之為漢陽王，南陽公袁恕己為南陽王，特進、同中書門下三品博陵公崔玄□為博陵王，罷知政事，賜金帛鞍馬，令朝朔望；

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Duke of Qi and Shizhong Jing Hui was made Prince of Pingyang, Duke of Qiao Huan Yuanfan Prince of Fuyang, Duke of Hanyang and Palace Attendant Zhang Jianzhi Prince of Hanyang, Duke of Nanyang Yuan Shuji Prince of Nanyang, and Special Advance Grandee and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin Duke of Boling Cui Xuanwei Prince of Boling; they ceased participation in government, were granted gold, silk, saddles, and horses, and were ordered to attend court on the new and full moon days;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Duke of Qi and Director of the Secretariat Jing Hui was made Prince of Pingyang, Duke of Qiao Huan Yuanfan Prince of Fuyang, Duke of Hanyang and Palace Attendant Zhang Jianzhi Prince of Hanyang, Duke of Nanyang Yuan Shuji Prince of Nanyang, and Special Advance Grandee and Grand Councilor Duke of Boling Cui Xuanwei Prince of Boling; they were removed from government, granted gold, silk, saddles, and horses, and ordered to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month;

sentences.zh: 仍賜彥范姓韋氏，與皇后同籍。

translations.literal: Yuanfan was further granted the surname Wei, sharing registry with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan was further granted the surname Wei and entered the same household register as the empress.

sentences.zh: 尋又以玄□檢校益州長史、知都督事，又改梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xuanwei was made Acting Chief Administrator of Yizhou and Supervisor of the Area Command, then transferred to Prefect of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xuanwei was made Acting Chief Administrator of Yizhou and put in charge of the area command, then transferred to Prefect of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三思令百官復修則天之政，不附武氏者斥之。

translations.literal: Sansi ordered the hundred officials to restore Empress Wu's policies; those who did not attach themselves to the Wu clan were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi ordered the officials to restore Empress Wu's policies; those who did not side with the Wu clan were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 為五王所逐者復之，大權盡歸三思矣。

translations.literal: Those whom the Five Kings had driven out were restored, and supreme power passed entirely to Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Those the Five Kings had driven out were restored, and supreme power passed entirely to Sansi.

sentences.zh: 五王之請削武氏諸王也，求人為表，眾莫肯為。

translations.literal: When the Five Kings requested the reduction of the Wu princes, they sought someone to draft the memorial, and none would do it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Kings asked that the Wu princes be reduced in rank, they sought someone to draft the memorial, and no one would do it.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人岑羲為之，語甚激切；

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Cen Xi did it for them, and the language was very forceful;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafting Officer Cen Xi drafted it for them, and the language was very forceful;

sentences.zh: 中書舍人偃師畢構次當讀表，辭色明厲。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Bi Gou of Yanshi, whose turn it was next to read the memorial, did so with bright and stern expression.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafting Officer Bi Gou of Yanshi, whose turn it was to read the memorial, did so with bright and stern expression.

sentences.zh: 三思既得志，羲改秘書少監，出構為潤州刺史。

translations.literal: After Sansi had gotten his way, Xi was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, and Gou was sent out as Prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sansi had gotten his way, Xi was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, and Gou was sent out as Prefect of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 易州刺史趙履溫，桓彥范之妻兄也。

translations.literal: Zhao Lüwen, Prefect of Yizhou, was the elder brother of Huan Yuanfan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüwen, Prefect of Yizhou, was the elder brother of Huan Yuanfan's wife.

sentences.zh: 彥范之誅二張，稱履溫預其謀，召為司農少卿，履溫以二婢遺彥范；

translations.literal: When Yuanfan executed the Two Zhangs, he claimed Lüwen had participated in the plot and summoned him as Deputy Minister of Public Works; Lüwen gave Yuanfan two maidservants;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanfan executed the Two Zhangs, he claimed Lüwen had shared in the plot and summoned him as Deputy Minister of Public Works; Lüwen gave Yuanfan two maidservants;

sentences.zh: 及彥范罷政事，履溫復奪其婢。

translations.literal: when Yuanfan ceased participation in government, Lüwen took the maidservants back again.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanfan was removed from government, Lüwen took the maidservants back.

sentences.zh: 上嘉宋璟忠直，屢遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Song Jing's loyalty and uprightness and repeatedly promoted him to Yellow Gate Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Song Jing's loyalty and uprightness and repeatedly promoted him to Yellow Gate Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 武三思嘗為事屬璟，璟正色拒之曰：「今太后既復子明辟，王當以侯就第，何得尚干朝政！

translations.literal: Wu Sansi once had a matter he wanted Song Jing to handle; Jing sternly refused him and said, "Now that the Empress Dowager has restored the son to illuminate the throne, Your Highness ought to take your marquisate and retire to your estate—how can you still meddle in court government!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi once wanted Song Jing to handle a matter for him; Jing sternly refused and said, "Now that the Empress Dowager has restored the son to the throne, Your Highness ought to take your marquisate and retire to your estate—how can you still meddle in court affairs!

sentences.zh: 獨不見產、祿之事乎？」

translations.literal: Have you alone not seen the affair of Chan and Lu?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen what became of Chan and Lu?

sentences.zh: 以韋安石兼檢校中書令，魏元忠兼檢校侍中，又以李湛為右散騎常侍，趙承恩為光祿卿，楊元琰為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Wei Anshi was additionally made Acting Palace Attendant, Wei Yuanzhong Acting Shizhong; Li Zhan was made Right Regular Attendant, Zhao Chengen Director of the Imperial Household, and Yang Yuanyan Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi was additionally made Acting Palace Attendant, Wei Yuanzhong Acting Director of the Secretariat; Li Zhan was made Right Regular Attendant, Zhao Chengen Director of the Imperial Household, and Yang Yuanyan Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，元琰知三思浸用事，請棄官為僧，上不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuanyan saw that Sansi was gradually gaining power in government and asked to abandon office and become a monk; the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuanyan saw that Sansi was gradually gaining power and asked to resign and become a monk; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 敬暉聞之，笑曰：「使我早知，勸上許之，髡去胡頭，豈不妙哉！」

translations.literal: When Jing Hui heard of it, he laughed and said, "Had I known earlier, I would have advised the emperor to grant it—shave off that Hu head, would that not have been splendid!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Hui heard of it, he laughed and said, "Had I known sooner, I would have urged the emperor to grant it—shave off that Hu head, would that not have been splendid!

sentences.zh: 元琰多須，類胡，故暉戲之。

translations.literal: Yuanyan had much facial hair and resembled a Hu, so Jing Hui jested at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan had heavy facial hair and looked like a Hu, so Jing Hui was teasing him.

sentences.zh: 元琰曰：「功成名遂，不退將危。

translations.literal: Yuanyan said, "When merit is achieved and fame fulfilled, not retiring will bring peril.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan said, "When merit is achieved and fame fulfilled, not retiring brings peril.

sentences.zh: 此乃由衷之請，非徒然也。」

translations.literal: This is a request from the heart, not an empty one."
translations.idiomatic: This is a sincere request from the heart, not an empty gesture.

sentences.zh: 暉知其意，瞿然不悅。

translations.literal: Jing Hui understood his meaning and was suddenly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui understood what he meant and was suddenly displeased.

sentences.zh: 及暉等得罪，元琰獨免。

translations.literal: When Jing Hui and the others were punished, Yuanyan alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Hui and the others were punished, Yuanyan alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 上官婕妤勸韋後襲則天故事，上表請天下士庶為出母服喪三年，又請百姓年二十三為丁，五十九免役，改易制度以收時望。

translations.literal: Consort Shangguan urged Empress Wei to follow Empress Wu's example: she submitted a memorial asking that scholars and commoners throughout the realm observe three years of mourning for birth mothers, and also asked that commoners be registered for corvée at age twenty-three and exempted at fifty-nine, altering institutions to win popular esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shangguan urged Empress Wei to follow Empress Wu's example: she memorialized asking that scholars and commoners throughout the realm observe three years of mourning for birth mothers, and also asked that commoners be registered for corvée at twenty-three and exempted at fifty-nine, changing institutions to win popular esteem.

sentences.zh: 制皆許之。

translations.literal: The edicts all granted these requests.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts granted all of it.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，制：降諸武，梁王三思為德靜王，定王攸暨為樂壽王，河內王懿宗等十二人皆降為公，以厭人心。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, an edict reduced the various Wus: Prince of Liang Wu Sansi was made Prince of Dejing, Prince of Ding Wu Youji Prince of Leshou, and Prince of Henei Wu Yizong and twelve others were all reduced to dukes, to satisfy popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, an edict reduced the Wu princes: Prince of Liang Wu Sansi was made Prince of Dejing, Prince of Ding Wu Youji Prince of Leshou, and Prince of Henei Wu Yizong and twelve others were all reduced to dukes, to satisfy popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以唐休璟為左僕射，同中書門下三品如故，豆盧欽望為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Tang Xiujing was made Left Vice Director, his Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin unchanged, and Dou Luqinwang was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Tang Xiujing was made Left Vice Director, remaining Grand Councilor as before, and Dou Luqinwang was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，以左驍衛大將軍裴思說充靈武軍大總管，以備突厥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renzi, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Pei Sishuo was appointed Grand Commander of the Lingwu Army to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Pei Sishuo was appointed Grand Commander of the Lingwu Army to guard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，命右僕射豆盧欽望，有軍國重事，中書門下可共平章。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Right Vice Director Dou Luqinwang was ordered that on weighty military and state affairs, the Secretariat and Chancellery might jointly decide them with him.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Right Vice Director Dou Luqinwang was ordered that on weighty military and state affairs, the Secretariat and Chancellery might jointly deliberate with him.

sentences.zh: 先是，僕射為正宰相，其後多兼中書門下之職，午前決朝政，午後決省事。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Vice Director had been the chief chancellor; afterward most also held Secretariat and Chancellery posts—before noon they decided court affairs, after noon they decided ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Vice Director had been the chief chancellor; later most also held Secretariat and Chancellery posts—before noon they decided court affairs, after noon ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 至是，欽望專為僕射，不敢預政事，故有是命。

translations.literal: At this time Qinwang held the Vice Directorship alone and dared not participate in government, hence this order.
translations.idiomatic: Now Qinwang held the Vice Directorship alone and dared not participate in government, hence this order.

sentences.zh: 是後專拜僕射者，不復為宰相矣。

translations.literal: After this, those appointed Vice Director alone were no longer chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: After this, those appointed Vice Director alone were no longer counted as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 又以韋安石為中書令，魏元忠為侍中，楊再思檢校為中書令。

translations.literal: Wei Anshi was again made Palace Attendant, Wei Yuanzhong Shizhong, and Yang Zaisi Acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi was again made Palace Attendant, Wei Yuanzhong Director of the Secretariat, and Yang Zaisi Acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，祔孝敬皇帝於太廟，號義宗。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Emperor Xiaojing was enshrined in the imperial ancestral temple, styled Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Emperor Xiaojing was enshrined in the imperial ancestral temple under the temple name Yizong.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，洛水溢，流二千餘家。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Luo River overflowed and swept away more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the Luo River overflowed and swept away more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛巳，以太子賓客韋巨源同中書門下三品，西京留守如故。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinsi, Heir Apparent's Guest Wei Juyuan was made Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin, his post as defender of the Western Capital unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinsi, Heir Apparent's Guest Wei Juyuan was made Grand Councilor, remaining defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 特進漢陽王張柬之表請歸襄州養疾；

translations.literal: Special Advance Grandee and Prince of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi memorialized requesting to return to Xiangzhou to nurse his illness;
translations.idiomatic: Special Advance Grandee and Prince of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi memorialized asking to return to Xiangzhou to nurse his illness;

sentences.zh: 乙未，以柬之為襄州刺史，不知州事，給全俸。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Jianzhi was made Prefect of Xiangzhou, not managing prefectural affairs, with full salary granted.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Jianzhi was made Prefect of Xiangzhou without managing prefectural affairs, with full salary granted.

sentences.zh: 河南、北十七州大水。

translations.literal: Seventeen prefectures north and south of the Yellow River suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen prefectures north and south of the Yellow River suffered severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊申，以水災求直言。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wushen, because of the flood disaster the emperor sought candid memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wushen, because of the floods the emperor sought candid memorials.

sentences.zh: 右衛騎曹參軍西河宋務光上疏，以為：「水陰類，臣妾之象，恐後庭有干外朝之政者，宜杜絕其萌。

translations.literal: Right Guard Cavalry Adjutant Song Wuguang of Xihe submitted a memorial, holding that: "Water belongs to the yin category and is the image of consorts and concubines; I fear there are those in the rear palace who meddle in outer-court government—their beginnings should be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Cavalry Adjutant Song Wuguang of Xihe submitted a memorial arguing: "Water belongs to the yin category and symbolizes consorts and concubines; I fear women of the rear palace are meddling in outer-court government—their influence should be cut off at the root.

sentences.zh: 今霖雨不止，乃閉坊門以禳之，至使里巷謂坊門為宰相，言朝廷使之燮理陰陽也。

translations.literal: Now the rains do not cease, yet ward gates are closed to exorcise the disaster, until the lanes and alleys call the ward gates the chancellors, saying the court makes them harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rains will not stop, yet ward gates are closed to exorcise the disaster, until people in the lanes call the ward gates the chancellors, saying the court makes them regulate yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 又，太子國本，宜早擇賢能而立之。

translations.literal: Further, the crown prince is the root of the state; a worthy and capable man should be chosen and established early.
translations.idiomatic: Further, the crown prince is the root of the state; a worthy and capable heir should be chosen and established early.

sentences.zh: 又，外戚太盛，如武三思等，宜解其機要，厚以祿賜。

translations.literal: Further, external kin are too powerful; men such as Wu Sansi should be removed from key posts and richly rewarded with stipends and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Further, the empress's kin are too powerful; men such as Wu Sansi should be removed from key posts and richly rewarded with stipends and gifts.

sentences.zh: 又，鄭普思、葉靜能以小技竊大位，亦朝政之蠹也。」

translations.literal: Further, Zheng Pusi and Ye Jingneng, by petty arts, stole high office—they too are pests of court government."
translations.idiomatic: Further, Zheng Pusi and Ye Jingneng stole high office through petty arts—they too are pests of court government.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and ignored.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，追立妃趙氏為恭皇后，孝敬皇帝妃裴氏為哀皇后。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Consort Zhao was posthumously established as Empress Gong, and Consort Pei, consort of Emperor Xiaojing, as Empress Ai.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Consort Zhao was posthumously honored as Empress Gong, and Consort Pei, consort of Emperor Xiaojing, as Empress Ai.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬午，上祀昊天上帝、皇地示氏於明堂，以高宗配。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day renwu, the emperor sacrificed to August Heaven and the Earth Spirit at the Bright Hall, with Emperor Gaozong as secondary offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renwu, the emperor sacrificed to August Heaven and the Earth Spirit at the Bright Hall, with Emperor Gaozong as secondary offering.

sentences.zh: 初，上在房陵，州司制約甚急；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at Fangling, the district offices' restrictions were very severe;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor was at Fangling, the district offices' restrictions were very severe;

sentences.zh: 刺史河東張知謇、靈昌崔敬嗣獨待遇以禮，供給豐贍，上德之，擢知謇自貝州刺史為左衛將軍，賜爵范陽公。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Zhiqie of Hedong and Cui Jingsi of Lingchang alone treated him with courtesy and supplied him abundantly; the emperor was grateful and promoted Zhiqie from Prefect of Beizhou to Left Guard General, granting him the title Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Zhiqie of Hedong and Cui Jingsi of Lingchang alone treated him with courtesy and supplied him generously; the emperor was grateful and promoted Zhiqie from Prefect of Beizhou to Left Guard General, granting him the title Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 敬嗣已卒，求得其子汪，嗜酒，不堪厘職，除五品散官。

translations.literal: Jingsi had already died; his son Wang was found—he was addicted to wine and unfit to manage office, so he was given a fifth-rank scattered office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsi had already died; his son Wang was found, but he was a drunkard and unfit for office, so he was given a fifth-rank sinecure.

sentences.zh: 改葬上洛王韋玄貞，其儀皆如太原王故事。

translations.literal: Prince Shangluo Wei Xuanzhen was reinterred; the rites all followed the precedent of the Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shangluo Wei Xuanzhen was reinterred with rites following the precedent of the Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，太子賓客、同中書門下三品韋巨源罷為禮部尚書，以其從父安石為中書令故也。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Heir Apparent's Guest and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin Wei Juyuan was removed and made Minister of Rites, because his father's younger brother Anshi was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Heir Apparent's Guest and Grand Councilor Wei Juyuan was removed and made Minister of Rites, because his father's younger brother Anshi was Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以左衛將軍上邽紀處訥兼檢校太府卿，處訥娶武三思之妻姊故也。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Ji Chunna of Shanggui was additionally made Acting Director of the Grand Treasury, because Chunna had married Wu Sansi's wife's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Ji Chunna of Shanggui was additionally made Acting Director of the Grand Treasury, because he had married Wu Sansi's wife's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，命唐休璟留守京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Tang Xiujing was ordered to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Tang Xiujing was ordered to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上幸龍門；

translations.literal: On the day guihai, the emperor visited Longmen;
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the emperor visited Longmen;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，獵於新安而還。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, he hunted at Xin'an and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, he hunted at Xin'an and returned.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以魏元忠為中書令，楊再思為侍中。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Wei Yuanzhong was made Palace Attendant and Yang Zaisi Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Wei Yuanzhong was made Palace Attendant and Yang Zaisi Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅，群臣上皇帝尊號曰應天皇帝，皇后曰順天皇后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day wuyin, the officials submitted an imperial honorific title to the emperor as Emperor Yingtian and to the empress as Empress Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuyin, the officials submitted honorific titles to the emperor as Emperor Yingtian and to the empress as Empress Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上與後謁謝太廟，赦天下；

translations.literal: On the day renwu, the emperor and empress visited the imperial ancestral temple to give thanks; an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the emperor and empress visited the imperial ancestral temple to give thanks; an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 相王、太平公主加實封，皆滿萬戶。

translations.literal: the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping received added fiefs, each reaching ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping received added fiefs, each reaching ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 己丑，上御洛城南樓，觀潑寒胡戲。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the emperor mounted the south tower of Luoyang to watch the Cold-Dispelling Hu play.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the emperor mounted the south tower of Luoyang to watch the Cold-Dispelling Hu performance.

sentences.zh: 清源尉呂元泰上疏，以為「謀時寒若，何必裸身揮水，鼓舞衢路以索之！」

translations.literal: Assistant Magistrate Lu Yuantai of Qingyuan submitted a memorial, holding that "to be anxious about the season's cold is enough—why must one bare the body and splash water, drumming and dancing in the public roads to seek it!"
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Magistrate Lu Yuantai of Qingyuan submitted a memorial arguing that "to care for the season's cold is enough—why bare the body and splash water, drumming and dancing in the public roads to seek relief!

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and rejected.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，則天崩於上陽宮，年八十二。

translations.literal: On the renyin day, Zetian passed away at Shangyang Palace, at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, Zetian died at Shangyang Palace at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 遺制：「去帝號，稱則天大聖皇后。

translations.literal: Her final edict: "Remove the imperial title; she shall be styled Empress Zetian the Great Sage.
translations.idiomatic: In her final edict she directed: "Let the imperial title be removed; let her be called Empress Zetian the Great Sage.

sentences.zh: 王、蕭二族及褚遂良、韓瑗、柳奭親屬皆赦之。」

translations.literal: The Wang and Xiao clans, and the relatives of Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and Liu Shi, were all pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The Wang and Xiao clans, together with the kinsmen of Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and Liu Shi, were all granted amnesty."

sentences.zh: 上居諒陰，以魏元忠攝塚宰三日。

translations.literal: The Emperor observed mourning in seclusion, appointing Wei Yuanzhong to serve as acting Grand Minister for three days.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong kept to his mourning seclusion, Wei Yuanzhong was appointed to act as Grand Minister for three days.

sentences.zh: 元忠素負忠直之望，中外賴之；

translations.literal: Yuanzhong had long borne the reputation of loyalty and integrity, and both within and outside the court relied upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong had long enjoyed a reputation for loyalty and forthrightness, and court and country alike looked to him;

sentences.zh: 武三思憚之，矯太后遺制，慰諭元忠，賜實封百戶。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi feared him, forged the Empress Dowager's final edict, comforted and reassured Yuanzhong, and granted him one hundred households of permanent enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, fearing him, forged Zetian's final edict to console Yuanzhong and bestow upon him a permanent fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 元忠捧制，感咽涕泗，見者曰：「事去矣！」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong received the edict and, overcome with emotion, wept aloud; those who witnessed it said: "The cause is lost!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong took the edict in his hands and, choking back sobs, wept openly; witnesses said: "All is lost!

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁卯，上始御同明殿見群臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the dingmao day, the Emperor first took the throne in Tongming Hall to receive the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the dingmao day, Zhongzong for the first time held audience with his ministers in Tongming Hall.

sentences.zh: 太后將合葬乾陵，給事中嚴善思上疏，以為：「乾陵玄宮以石為門，鐵錮其縫，今啟其門，必須鐫鑿。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was about to be interred together with the late emperor at Qianling. Supervising Secretary Yan Shansi submitted a memorial, stating: "The inner chamber of Qianling has stone for its doors, with iron sealing the seams; to open them now would require carving and chiseling.
translations.idiomatic: As plans were made to bury Zetian together with Gaozong at Qianling, Supervising Secretary Yan Shansi submitted a memorial arguing: "The inner chamber of Qianling is sealed with stone doors bound in iron; opening them now would require forceful carving and chiseling.

sentences.zh: 神明之道，體尚幽玄，動眾加功，恐多驚黷。

translations.literal: The way of the spirits reveres what is hidden and profound; to mobilize the multitude and add labor would, I fear, cause much disturbance and profanation.
translations.idiomatic: The realm of the spirits cherishes stillness and mystery; to muster a crowd and set them to work would, I fear, profane what should remain undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 況合葬非古，漢時諸陵，皇后多不合陵，魏、晉已降，始有合者。

translations.literal: Moreover, joint burial is not the ancient custom; in the Han, at most imperial tombs, empresses were mostly not buried together with the emperor; only from Wei and Jin downward did joint burial begin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, joint burial is not the ancient way: under the Han, empresses were usually buried apart from their emperors; only from Wei and Jin onward did the practice of shared tombs arise.

sentences.zh: 望於乾陵之傍更擇吉地為陵，若神道有知，幽塗自當通會；

translations.literal: I hope that a separate auspicious site may be chosen beside Qianling for her tomb; if the spirit path has awareness, the dark road will naturally join them;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an auspicious site be chosen near Qianling for a separate tomb; if the spirits are aware, their paths in the underworld will surely meet;

sentences.zh: 若其無知，合之何益！」

translations.literal: If they have no awareness, what benefit is there in joining them together!
translations.idiomatic: and if they are not aware, what good would joint burial do?

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: End of memorial." His advice was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: End of memorial." The request was rejected.

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部奏天下戶六百一十五萬，口三千七百一十四萬有畸。

translations.literal: That year, the Ministry of Revenue reported that under Heaven there were six million one hundred fifty thousand households and thirty-seven million one hundred forty thousand persons and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported sixty-one million five hundred thousand households and thirty-seven million one hundred forty-odd persons throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊戌，以吏部尚書李嶠同中書門下三品，中書侍郎-{于}-惟謙同平章事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the wuxu day, Minister of Civil Appointments Li Qiao was made Associate Grand Counselor of the Chancellery and Secretariat of the Third Rank, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Weiqian was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the wuxu day of the first month, Li Qiao, Minister of Civil Appointments, was appointed Associate Grand Counselor of the Third Rank, and Yu Weiqian, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙午，制：「太平、長安、安樂、宜城、新都、定安、金城公主並開府，置官屬。」

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the bingwu day, an edict stated: "The Princesses Taiping, Chang'an, Anle, Yicheng, Xindu, Ding'an, and Jincheng shall all establish households with official staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the bingwu day, an edict declared: "The Princesses Taiping, Chang'an, Anle, Yicheng, Xindu, Ding'an, and Jincheng shall each establish a household office and appoint a full staff.

sentences.zh: 武三思以敬暉、桓彥范、袁恕己尚在京師，忌之，乙卯，出為滑、洺、豫三州刺史。

translations.literal: Because Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and Yuan Shuji were still in the capital, Wu Sansi resented them; on the yimao day, they were sent out as prefects of Hua, Ming, and Yu respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, resenting that Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and Yuan Shuji still remained in the capital, had them transferred on the yimao day to serve as prefects of Hua, Ming, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 賜閺鄉僧萬回號法雲公。

translations.literal: The monk Wan Hui of Min Township was granted the title Duke of Fayun.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Wan Hui of Min Township was given the title Duke of Fayun.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以突騎施酋長烏質勒為懷德郡王。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, Wuzhile, chieftain of the Turgesh, was made Prince of Huaidé Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day, Wuzhile, chieftain of the Turgesh, was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaidé Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，以刑部尚書韋巨源同中書門下三品，仍與皇后敘宗族。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the ywei day, Minister of Justice Wei Juyuan was made Associate Grand Counselor of the Third Rank, and was also granted a reckoning of clan relationship with the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the ywei day, Wei Juyuan, Minister of Justice, was appointed Associate Grand Counselor of the Third Rank and formally acknowledged as a kinsman of the Empress.

sentences.zh: 丙申，僧慧范等九人並加五品階，賜爵郡、縣公；

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, the nine monks including Huifan were all promoted by five ranks and granted titles of commandery or county duke;
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, the nine monks including Huifan were each raised five ranks and ennobled as commandery or county dukes;

sentences.zh: 道士史崇恩等三人加五品階，除國子祭酒，同正；

translations.literal: the three Daoist masters including Shi Chong'en were promoted by five ranks, appointed Rectors of the Directorate of Education with full status;
translations.idiomatic: the three Daoist masters including Shi Chong'en were raised five ranks and appointed Rectors of the Directorate of Education with full standing;

sentences.zh: 葉靜能加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Ye Jingneng was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Jingneng was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 選左、右台及內外五品以上官二十人為十道巡察使，委之察吏撫人，薦賢直獄，二年一代，考其功罪而進退之。

translations.literal: Twenty officials of the fifth rank and above from the Left and Right Censorates and from within and outside the capital were selected as ten-circuit inspection commissioners, entrusted to inspect officials and comfort the people, recommend the worthy and rectify prisons; they would serve two years per term, and be promoted or demoted according to their merit and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty officials of the fifth rank and above from the Left and Right Censorates and from court and provinces were chosen as ten-circuit inspection commissioners, charged with scrutinizing officials, comforting the people, recommending talent, and correcting judicial abuses; each would serve a two-year term, after which promotion or dismissal would follow their record of achievement and failure.

sentences.zh: 易州刺史魏人姜師度、禮部員外郎馬懷素、殿中侍御史臨漳源乾曜、監察御史靈昌盧懷慎、衛尉少卿滏陽李傑皆預焉。

translations.literal: Among them were Prefect of Yizhou Jiang Shidu of Wei, Vice Minister of Rites Ma Huaisu, Palace Attendant Censor Yuan Gan'yao of Linzhang, Investigating Censor Lu Huaizhen of Lingchang, and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Li Jie of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Those appointed included Jiang Shidu of Wei, prefect of Yizhou; Ma Huaisu, Vice Minister of Rites; Yuan Gan'yao of Linzhang, Palace Attendant Censor; Lu Huaizhen of Lingchang, Investigating Censor; and Li Jie of Fuyang, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲辰，中書令韋安石罷為戶部尚書；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the jiachen day, Chief Minister of the Secretariat Wei Anshi was removed and made Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the jiachen day, Wei Anshi was dismissed as Chief Minister of the Secretariat and appointed Minister of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書蘇瑰為侍中、西京留守。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Su Gui was made Palace Attendant and Protector-General of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui, Minister of Revenue, was appointed Palace Attendant and Protector-General of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 瑰，頲之父也。

translations.literal: Gui was the father of Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui was the father of Su Ting.

sentences.zh: 唐休璟致仕。

translations.literal: Tang Xiujing retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing retired from office.

sentences.zh: 初，少府監丞弘農宋之問及弟兗州司倉之遜皆坐附會張易之貶嶺南，逃歸東都，匿於友人光祿卿、駙馬都尉王同皎家。

translations.literal: Earlier, Assistant Director of the Palace Storehouses Song Zhiwen of Hongnong and his younger brother Zhixun, Warehouse Clerk of Yanzhou, had both been punished for associating with Zhang Yizhi and exiled to Lingnan; they fled back to the Eastern Capital and hid in the home of their friend Wang Tongjiao, Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Guard.
