translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Song Zhiwen of Hongnong, Assistant Director of the Palace Storehouses, and his younger brother Zhixun, warehouse clerk of Yanzhou, had both been banished to Lingnan for their association with Zhang Yizhi; they escaped back to the Eastern Capital and took refuge with their friend Wang Tongjiao, Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Guard.

sentences.zh: 同皎疾武三思及韋後所為，每與所親言之，輒切齒。

translations.literal: Tongjiao detested the conduct of Wu Sansi and Empress Wei; whenever he spoke of it to those close to him, he would gnash his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjiao loathed the conduct of Wu Sansi and Empress Wei, and whenever he spoke of it among his intimates he would grind his teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 之遜於簾下聞之，密遣其子曇及甥校書郎李悛告三思，欲以自贖。

translations.literal: Zhixun overheard this from behind a curtain and secretly sent his son Tan and his nephew, Collator Li Quan, to inform Sansi, hoping thereby to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun overheard this from behind a curtain and secretly sent his son Tan and his nephew Li Quan, a collator, to inform Wu Sansi, hoping to win pardon for himself.

sentences.zh: 三思使曇、悛及撫州司倉冉祖雍上書告同皎與洛陽人張仲之、祖延慶、武當丞壽春周憬等潛結壯士，謀殺三思，因勒兵詣闕，廢皇后。

translations.literal: Sansi had Tan, Quan, and Ran Zuyong, Warehouse Clerk of Fuzhou, submit a memorial accusing Tongjiao, together with Zhang Zhongzhi of Luoyang, Zu Yanqing, and Zhou Jing of Shouchun, Assistant Magistrate of Wudang, of secretly gathering strong men, plotting to kill Sansi, then leading troops to the palace to depose the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi had Tan, Quan, and Ran Zuyong, warehouse clerk of Fuzhou, submit a memorial accusing Tongjiao, together with Zhang Zhongzhi of Luoyang, Zu Yanqing, and Zhou Jing of Shouchun, assistant magistrate of Wudang, of secretly recruiting strong men to kill Sansi, then marching on the palace to depose the Empress.

sentences.zh: 上命御史大夫李承嘉、監察御史姚紹之按其事，又命楊再思、李嶠、韋巨源參驗。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi to investigate the matter, and also ordered Yang Zaisi, Li Qiao, and Wei Juyuan to assist in the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi to investigate the case, with Yang Zaisi, Li Qiao, and Wei Juyuan appointed to assist in the review.

sentences.zh: 仲之言三思罪狀，事連宮壺。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi spoke of Sansi's crimes, and the affair touched the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi denounced Wu Sansi's crimes, implicating the inner palace in the affair.

sentences.zh: 再思、巨源陽寐不聽；

translations.literal: Zaisi and Juyuan feigned sleep and would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi and Juyuan pretended to doze and refused to listen;

sentences.zh: 嶠與紹之命反接送獄。

translations.literal: Qiao and Shaozhi ordered him bound and sent back to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiao and Yao Shaozhi ordered him seized and returned to prison.

sentences.zh: 仲之還顧，言不已。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi turned back and looked behind him, still speaking without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi looked back over his shoulder and continued shouting without pause.

sentences.zh: 紹之命撾之，折其臂。

translations.literal: Shaozhi ordered him beaten with clubs, breaking his arm.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shaozhi ordered him beaten with clubs until his arm was broken.

sentences.zh: 仲之大呼曰：「吾已負汝，死當訟汝於天！」

translations.literal: Zhongzhi cried out loudly: "I have already been wronged by you; when I die I shall bring suit against you before Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi cried out: "You have already wronged me; when I die I shall accuse you before Heaven!

sentences.zh: 庚戌，同皎等皆坐斬，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: End of speech." On the gengxu day, Tongjiao and the others were all executed by decapitation, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." On the gengxu day, Tongjiao and his associates were all beheaded, and their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 周憬亡入比干廟中，大言曰：「比干古之忠臣，知吾此心！

translations.literal: Zhou Jing fled into the Temple of Bi Gan and cried out: "Bi Gan was a loyal minister of old; know my heart!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing fled into the Temple of Bi Gan and cried aloud: "Bi Gan was a loyal minister of antiquity—know what is in my heart!

sentences.zh: 三思與皇后淫亂，傾危國家，行當梟首都市，恨不及見耳！」

translations.literal: Sansi and the Empress commit lewd disorder, endangering the state; soon their heads will be displayed in the capital market—I regret only that I shall not live to see it!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi and the Empress have debauched the court and brought the realm to ruin; soon their heads will hang in the capital marketplace—I regret only that I shall not live to see it!

sentences.zh: 遂自剄。

translations.literal: End of speech." He then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." Then he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 之問、之遜、曇、悛、祖雍並除京官，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Zhiwen, Zhixun, Tan, Quan, and Zuyong were all appointed to capital offices and promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen, Zhixun, Tan, Quan, and Zuyong were all appointed to offices in the capital and promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 武三思與韋後日夜譖敬暉等不已，復左遷暉為朗州刺史，崔玄暐為均州刺史，桓彥范為亳州刺史，袁恕己為郢州刺史；

translations.literal: Wu Sansi and Empress Wei day and night slandered Jing Hui and the others without cease, and again demoted Hui to Prefect of Langzhou, Cui Xuanwei to Prefect of Junzhou, Huan Yanfan to Prefect of Bozhou, and Yuan Shuji to Prefect of Yingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi and Empress Wei ceaselessly slandered Jing Hui and his allies, and had them demoted once more: Hui to prefect of Langzhou, Cui Xuanwei to prefect of Junzhou, Huan Yanfan to prefect of Bozhou, and Yuan Shuji to prefect of Yingzhou;

sentences.zh: 與暉等同立功者謝思行等皆以為黨與，坐貶。

translations.literal: Xie Sixing and others who had shared in Hui's meritorious deed were all treated as partisans and punished with demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Sixing and others who had shared in Hui's coup were all treated as accomplices and demoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 大置員外官，自京司及諸州凡二千餘人，宦官超遷七品以上員外官者又將千人。

translations.literal: Extra officials were appointed on a large scale; from the capital offices and the various prefectures there were more than two thousand in all, and among eunuchs promoted by extraordinary advancement to extra offices of the seventh rank and above there were nearly a thousand more.
translations.idiomatic: Extra officials were created in great numbers: more than two thousand in the capital and the provinces combined, with nearly a thousand eunuchs alone advanced by irregular promotion to extra posts of the seventh rank and above.

sentences.zh: 魏元忠自端州還，為相，不復強諫，惟與時俯仰，中外失望。

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong returned from Duanzhou and became Chancellor, but no longer remonstrated forcefully; he merely adjusted himself to the times, and both within and outside the court were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong returned from exile in Duanzhou and again became Chancellor, but he no longer remonstrated boldly; he merely bent with the times, and court and country alike were disheartened.

sentences.zh: 酸棗尉袁楚客致書元忠，以為：「主上新服厥命，惟新厥德，當進君子，退小人，以興大化，豈可安其榮寵，循默而已！

translations.literal: Yuan Chuke, magistrate of Suanzao, wrote to Yuanzhong, stating: "Our lord has newly assumed his mandate and should renew his virtue; he ought to advance gentlemen and dismiss petty men to bring about great transformation—how can one rest content in rank and favor and remain silent!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chuke, magistrate of Suanzao, wrote to Yuanzhong arguing: "The Emperor has newly assumed the throne and should renew his virtue; he ought to elevate the worthy and remove the base to bring about great reform—how can you rest content in honor and silence!

sentences.zh: 今不早建太子，擇師傅而輔之，一失也。

translations.literal: Now, not establishing the Crown Prince early and choosing tutors to assist him—this is the first failure.
translations.idiomatic: First failure: the Crown Prince has not yet been established early, with tutors chosen to guide him.

sentences.zh: 公主開府置僚屬，二失也。

translations.literal: Princesses establishing households and appointing staffs—this is the second failure.
translations.idiomatic: Second failure: princesses have been allowed to establish household offices and appoint their own staffs.

sentences.zh: 崇長緇衣，使遊走權門，借勢納賂，三失也。

translations.literal: Honoring monks in black robes and letting them roam among powerful gates, borrowing influence to accept bribes—this is the third failure.
translations.idiomatic: Third failure: Buddhist monks are honored and allowed to haunt the doors of the powerful, trading on influence to accept bribes.

sentences.zh: 俳優小人，盜竊品秩，四失也。

translations.literal: Entertainers and petty men steal ranks and grades—this is the fourth failure.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth failure: actors and other base men have stolen official rank.

sentences.zh: 有司選進賢才，皆以貨取勢求，五失也。

translations.literal: When the responsible offices select and advance talented men, all do so by wealth and by seeking power—this is the fifth failure.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth failure: when offices select talent, they do so by bribery and by trading on influence.

sentences.zh: 寵進宦者，殆滿千人，為長亂之階，六失也。

translations.literal: Favored eunuchs promoted number nearly a full thousand, forming the steps to long disorder—this is the sixth failure.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth failure: favored eunuchs now number nearly a thousand, laying the groundwork for lasting turmoil.

sentences.zh: 王公貴戚，賞賜無度，競為侈靡，七失也。

translations.literal: Princes, dukes, and noble kin receive rewards without limit and vie in extravagance—this is the seventh failure.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh failure: princes and noble kin receive boundless rewards and compete in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 廣置員外官，傷財害民，八失也。

translations.literal: Extra officials are broadly appointed, wasting wealth and harming the people—this is the eighth failure.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth failure: the proliferation of extra officials drains the treasury and harms the people.

sentences.zh: 先朝宮女，得自便居外，出入無禁，交通請謁，九失也。

translations.literal: Palace women of the former reign are allowed to live outside at will, coming and going without restriction and conducting solicitations—this is the ninth failure.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth failure: palace women of the previous reign live freely outside the palace, coming and going without restraint and trading in petitions and favors.

sentences.zh: 左道之人，熒惑主聽，盜竊祿位，十失也。

translations.literal: Men of heterodox ways beguile the ruler's hearing and steal salary and position—this is the tenth failure.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth failure: heterodox adepts beguile the Emperor's ear and steal rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 凡此十失，君侯不正，誰正之哉！」

translations.literal: Of these ten failures, if you, my lord, do not set them right, who will set them right!
translations.idiomatic: Of these ten failures, if you will not set them right, who will?

sentences.zh: 元忠得書，愧謝而已。

translations.literal: End of letter." When Yuanzhong received the letter, he could only apologize in shame.
translations.idiomatic: End of letter." Yuanzhong received the letter and could only reply with shamefaced thanks.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，改贈後父韋玄貞為酆王，後四弟皆贈郡王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Empress's deceased father Wei Xuanzhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Feng, and her four younger brothers were all posthumously enfeoffed as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Empress's late father Wei Xuanzhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Feng, and her four younger brothers were all posthumously made commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 己丑，左散騎常侍、同中書門下三品李懷遠致仕。

translations.literal: On the jichou day, Left Regular Attendant and Associate Grand Counselor of the Third Rank Li Huaiyuan retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day, Li Huaiyuan, Left Regular Attendant and Associate Grand Counselor of the Third Rank, retired from office.

sentences.zh: 處士京兆韋月將上書告武三思潛通宮掖，必為逆亂；

translations.literal: The recluse Wei Yuejiang of Jingzhao submitted a memorial accusing Wu Sansi of secretly communicating with the inner palace and certain to bring rebellion and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Wei Yuejiang of Jingzhao submitted a memorial accusing Wu Sansi of secret dealings with the inner palace and warning that rebellion would surely follow;

sentences.zh: 上大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was furious and ordered his immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宋璟奏請推按，上益怒，不及整巾，屣履出側門，謂璟曰：「朕謂已斬，乃猶未邪！」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery Song Jing memorialized requesting a formal investigation; the Emperor grew still angrier, and without straightening his headcloth, went out the side gate in his slippers and said to Jing: "I thought he had already been executed—he is still not dead!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chancellery Song Jing petitioned for a formal investigation; Zhongzong grew still angrier, and without straightening his headcloth rushed out the side gate in his slippers, crying to Song Jing: "I thought he was already dead—is he still alive!

sentences.zh: 命趨斬之。

translations.literal: End of speech." He ordered that the execution be hurried.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." He ordered the execution carried out at once.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「人言中宮私於三思，陛下不問而誅之，臣恐天下必有竊議。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "People say the inner palace has private relations with Sansi; if Your Majesty executes him without inquiry, I fear there will surely be whispered talk throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing said: "People say the Empress has improper relations with Wu Sansi; if Your Majesty executes the accuser without investigation, I fear the realm will murmur against it.

sentences.zh: 固請按之，上不許。

translations.literal: End of speech." He firmly requested an investigation, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." He pressed for an investigation, but Zhongzong refused.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「必欲斬月將，請先斬臣！

translations.literal: Jing said: "If you must execute Yuejiang, please execute me first!
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing said: "If Yuejiang must die, execute me first!

sentences.zh: 不然，臣終不敢奉詔！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, I dare not in the end obey the edict!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I cannot obey Your Majesty's command!

sentences.zh: 上怒少解。

translations.literal: End of speech." The Emperor's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." Zhongzong's rage subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 左御史大夫蘇珦、給事中徐堅、大理卿長安尹思貞皆以為方夏行戮，有違時令。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Su Xian, Supervising Secretary Xu Jian, and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yin Sizhen of Chang'an all held that to carry out execution in midsummer would violate the seasonal ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Su Xian, Supervising Secretary Xu Jian, and Chief Judge Yin Sizhen of Chang'an all argued that execution in midsummer would violate seasonal propriety.

sentences.zh: 上乃命與杖，流嶺南。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered that he be beaten with the staff and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong then ordered him beaten with the staff and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 過秋分一日，平曉，廣州都督周仁軌斬之。

translations.literal: One day after the autumn equinox, at daybreak, Protector-General of Guangzhou Zhou Ren'gui executed him by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: One day after the autumn equinox, at daybreak, Zhou Ren'gui, Protector-General of Guangzhou, beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李承嘉附武三思，詆尹思貞於朝，思貞曰：「公附會奸臣，將圖不軌，先除忠臣邪！」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia, aligned with Wu Sansi, slandered Yin Sizhen at court; Sizhen said: "You align with treacherous ministers and plot sedition—do you mean first to remove loyal ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia, allied with Wu Sansi, slandered Yin Sizhen at court; Yin Sizhen replied: "You attach yourself to treacherous ministers and plot rebellion—is your first move to remove loyal men!

sentences.zh: 承嘉怒，劾奏思貞，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: End of speech." Chengjia was enraged, impeached and memorialized against Sizhen, and had him sent out as Prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." Chengjia, enraged, impeached Yin Sizhen and had him transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 或謂思貞曰：「公平日訥於言，及廷折承嘉，何其敏邪？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Sizhen: "You are usually slow of speech; when you rebutted Chengjia at court, how swift you were!
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Yin Sizhen: "You are usually slow of speech—how did you rebut Chengjia in court with such swiftness?

sentences.zh: 思貞曰：「物不能鳴者，激之則鳴。

translations.literal: End of speech." Sizhen said: "Things that cannot sound, when struck will sound.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech." Yin Sizhen replied: "Things that cannot sound will sound when struck.

sentences.zh: 承嘉恃威權相陵，僕義不受屈，亦不知言之從何而至也。」

translations.literal: Chengjia relied on power and authority to bully me; I, by principle, would not submit; I also do not know whence the words came.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia bullied me with his power; by principle I would not yield—and I cannot say where the words came from.

sentences.zh: 武三思惡宋璟，出之檢校貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi hated Song Jing and sent him out as acting Prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, resenting Song Jing, had him transferred to serve as acting prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚申，葬則天大聖皇后於乾陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the gengshen day, Empress Zetian the Great Sage was buried at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the gengshen day, Empress Zetian the Great Sage was interred at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 武三思使鄭愔告朗州刺史敬暉、亳州刺史韋彥范、襄州刺史張柬之、郢州刺史袁恕己、均州刺史崔玄暐與王同皎通謀。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi had Zheng Yin accuse Prefect of Langzhou Jing Hui, Prefect of Bozhou Wei Yanfan, Prefect of Xiangzhou Zhang Jianzhi, Prefect of Yingzhou Yuan Shuji, and Prefect of Junzhou Cui Xuanwei of conspiring with Wang Tongjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi had Zheng Yin accuse Jing Hui, prefect of Langzhou; Wei Yanfan, prefect of Bozhou; Zhang Jianzhi, prefect of Xiangzhou; Yuan Shuji, prefect of Yingzhou; and Cui Xuanwei, prefect of Junzhou, of conspiracy with Wang Tongjiao.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊寅，貶暉崖州司馬，彥范瀧州司馬，柬之新州司馬，恕己竇州司馬，玄暐白州司馬，並員外置，仍長任，削其勳封；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the wuyin day, Hui was demoted to Vice Prefect of Yazhou, Yanfan to Vice Prefect of Longzhou, Jianzhi to Vice Prefect of Xizhou, Shuji to Vice Prefect of Douzhou, and Xuanwei to Vice Prefect of Baizhou; all were appointed as extra officials with long-term tenure, and their meritorious enfeoffments were stripped;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the wuyin day, Hui was demoted to vice prefect of Yazhou, Yanfan to vice prefect of Longzhou, Jianzhi to vice prefect of Xizhou, Shuji to vice prefect of Douzhou, and Cui Xuanwei to vice prefect of Baizhou; all were appointed as supernumerary officials with indefinite tenure, and their honors and fiefs were revoked;

sentences.zh: 復彥范姓桓氏。

translations.literal: Yanfan's surname was restored to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan's original surname, Huan, was restored.

sentences.zh: 初，韋玄貞流欽州而卒，蠻酋寧承基兄弟逼取其女，妻崔氏不與，承基等殺之，及其四男洵、浩、洞、泚，上命廣州都督周仁軌使將兵二萬討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Xuanzhen had been exiled to Qinzhou and died there; the barbarian chieftain Ning Chengji and his brothers forced away his daughter; his wife, née Cui, would not yield, and Chengji and the others killed her, together with her four sons Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci; the Emperor ordered Protector-General of Guangzhou Zhou Ren'gui to lead twenty thousand troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Xuanzhen had died in exile at Qinzhou; the barbarian chieftain Ning Chengji and his brothers tried to seize his daughter by force; his wife, Lady Cui, refused, and they killed her along with her four sons Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci; Zhongzong ordered Zhou Ren'gui, Protector-General of Guangzhou, to lead twenty thousand troops against them.

sentences.zh: 承基等亡入海，仁軌追斬之，以其首祭崔氏墓，殺掠其部眾殆盡。

translations.literal: Chengji and the others fled into the sea; Ren'gui pursued and executed them, using their heads to sacrifice at Lady Cui's tomb, and killed and plundered their tribesmen nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Chengji and his followers fled to sea; Ren'gui pursued them, cut them down, and offered their heads at Lady Cui's tomb, slaughtering and plundering their followers nearly to the last.

sentences.zh: 上喜，加仁軌鎮國大將軍，充五府大使，賜爵汝南郡公。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased, promoted Ren'gui to Defender-in-Chief of the State, appointed him Commissioner of the Five Prefectorates, and granted him the title Duke of Runan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was delighted, promoted Ren'gui to Defender-in-Chief of the State, appointed him Commissioner of the Five Prefectures, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Runan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 韋後隔簾拜仁軌，以父事之。

translations.literal: Empress Wei received Ren'gui from behind a curtain and treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei received Ren'gui from behind a screen and honored him as a father.

sentences.zh: 及韋後敗，仁軌以黨與誅。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei later fell, Ren'gui was executed as an associate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei later fell, Ren'gui was executed as her accomplice.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊申，立衛王重俊為皇太子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the wushen day, Prince of Wei Chongjun was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the wushen day of the seventh month, Prince Chongjun of Wei was installed as Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子性明果，而官屬率貴遊子弟，所為多不法；

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was by nature bright and resolute, but his staff were mostly the sons of noble pleasure-seekers, and their conduct was largely unlawful;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was bright and resolute by nature, but his staff were mostly the sons of idle nobles, and their conduct was often lawless;

sentences.zh: 左庶子姚珽屢諫，不聽，珽，璹之弟也。

translations.literal: Left Mentor Yao Ting remonstrated repeatedly, but was not heeded; Ting was the younger brother of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Left Mentor Yao Ting remonstrated repeatedly, but was ignored; Yao Ting was the younger brother of Yao Shu.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以李嶠為中書令。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day, Li Qiao was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Li Qiao was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上將還西京，辛未，左散騎常侍李懷遠同中書門下三品，充東都留守。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to return to the Western Capital. On the day xinwei, Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Huaiyuan, with the third rank of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was appointed to serve as Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor prepared to return to Chang'an, on the day xinwei he appointed Li Huaiyuan—Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and a third-rank minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery—to remain behind as Defender of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 武三思陰令人疏皇后穢行，榜於天津橋，請加廢黜。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi secretly had someone draft a memorial denouncing the Empress's immoral conduct, posted it at Tianjin Bridge, and requested that she be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi secretly arranged for a denunciation of Empress Wei's scandalous conduct to be posted at Tianjin Bridge, calling for her deposition.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，命御史大夫李承嘉窮核其事。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to investigate the matter exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong flew into a rage and ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to pursue the affair to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 承嘉奏言：「敬暉、桓彥范、張柬之、袁恕己、崔玄暐使人為之，雖雲廢後，實謀大逆，請族誅之。」

translations.literal: Chengjia memorialized: "Jing Hui, Huan Yuanfan, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji, and Cui Xuanwei had men act for them; though they said they deposed the empress, in truth they plotted great treason—I beg that their clans be exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia reported: "Hui, Yuanfan, Jianzhi, Shuji, and Xuanwei had agents carry this out; though they claimed only to depose the empress, they in fact plotted rebellion. I beg that their entire clans be executed."

sentences.zh: 三思又使安樂公主譖之於內，侍御史鄭愔言之於外，上命法司結竟。

translations.literal: End of speech. Wu Sansi also had Princess Anle slander them within the palace, and Attending Censor Zheng Yin speak of it outside; the Emperor ordered the judicial authorities to conclude the case.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Wu Sansi meanwhile had Princess Anle whisper accusations against them inside the palace, while Attending Censor Zheng Yin aired the charges in public. Zhongzong ordered the courts to bring the case to a final judgment.

sentences.zh: 大理丞三原李朝隱奏稱：「暉等未經推鞫，不可遽就誅夷。」

translations.literal: Grand Court of Judicature Assistant Li Chaoyin of Sanyuan submitted: "Hui and the others have not yet undergone interrogation; they cannot abruptly be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin, an assistant in the Grand Court of Judicature from Sanyuan, argued: "Hui and his fellows have not even been interrogated—they must not be hurried to execution."

sentences.zh: 大理丞裴談奏稱：「暉等宜據制書處斬籍沒，不應更加推鞫。」

translations.literal: End of speech. Grand Court of Judicature Assistant Pei Tan submitted: "Hui and the others ought to be executed and their property confiscated according to the imperial decree; there should be no further interrogation."
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Pei Tan, another court assistant, countered: "The imperial decree already calls for their execution and the seizure of their estates. There is no need for further inquiry."

sentences.zh: 上以暉等嘗賜鐵券，許以不死，乃長流暉於瓊州，彥范於瀼州，柬之於瀧州，恕己於環州，玄暐於古州，子弟年十六以上，皆流嶺外。

translations.literal: End of speech. The Emperor, recalling that Hui and the others had once been granted iron certificates promising they would not be put to death, instead exiled Hui to Qiongzhou, Yanfan to Rangzhou, Jianzhi to Longzhou, Shuji to Huanzhou, and Xuanwei to Guzhou; all sons and younger brothers aged sixteen and above were likewise banished beyond the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Mindful that the five men had once received iron certificates guaranteeing their lives, Zhongzong spared them death but banished Hui to Qiongzhou, Yanfan to Rangzhou, Jianzhi to Longzhou, Shuji to Huanzhou, and Xuanwei to Guzhou. Every son and younger brother over sixteen was sent into exile beyond the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 擢承嘉為金紫光祿大夫，進爵襄武郡公，談為刑部尚書；

translations.literal: Chengjia was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and advanced in rank to Duke of Xiangwu Commandery; Pei Tan was made Minister of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia was raised to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and created Duke of Xiangwu; Pei Tan was appointed Minister of Justice;

sentences.zh: 出李朝隱為聞喜令。

translations.literal: Li Chaoyin was sent out to serve as Magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin was demoted and sent out to serve as magistrate of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 三思又諷太子上表，請夷暉等三族，上不許。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi also prompted the Crown Prince to submit a memorial requesting the extermination of the three clans of Hui and the others; the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi also induced the Crown Prince to memorial the throne, asking that Hui and his allies be wiped out to the third generation. Zhongzong refused.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人崔湜說三思曰：「暉等異日北歸，終為後患，不如遣使矯制殺之。」

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Cui Shi said to Wu Sansi: "If Hui and the others ever return north in the future, they will ultimately become a lingering threat. It would be better to dispatch an envoy with a forged imperial order to kill them."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafting Officer Cui Shi urged Wu Sansi: "If those men ever make their way back north, they will haunt us forever. Better to send an agent bearing a forged imperial order and finish them off."

sentences.zh: 三思問誰可使者，湜薦大理正周利用。

translations.literal: End of speech. Wu Sansi asked who could be sent; Cui Shi recommended Grand Court of Judicature Director Zhou Liyong.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Wu Sansi asked whom he could send. Cui Shi recommended Zhou Liyong, a director in the Grand Court of Judicature.

sentences.zh: 利用先為五王所惡，貶嘉州司馬，乃以利用攝右台侍御史，奉使嶺外。

translations.literal: Liyong had earlier been despised by the Five Princes and demoted to Military Assistant of Jia Prefecture. He was now appointed Acting Attending Censor of the Right Censorate and sent on a mission beyond the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong had long been hated by the Five Princes and had been banished to a post as military assistant in Jia Prefecture. Wu Sansi now gave him an acting appointment as Attending Censor of the Right Censorate and dispatched him beyond the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 比至，柬之、玄暐已死，遇彥范於貴州，令左右縛之，曳於竹槎之上，肉盡至骨，然後杖殺。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Jianzhi and Xuanwei were already dead. Encountering Yanfan in Guizhou, he had his attendants bind him, drag him over a bamboo sledge until his flesh was scraped to the bone, and then beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Jianzhi and Xuanwei were already dead. In Guizhou he caught Yanfan, had his men bind him and haul him over a bamboo sledge until the flesh was torn from his bones, then beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 得暉，咼而殺之。

translations.literal: Capturing Hui, he cut open his mouth and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he seized Hui, he sliced open his mouth and killed him.

sentences.zh: 恕己素服黃金，利用逼之使飲野葛汁，盡數升不死，不勝毒憤，掊地，爪甲殆盡，仍捶殺之。

translations.literal: Shuji habitually wore gold in his belt. Liyong forced him to drink kudzu-root poison; he consumed several sheng without dying. Unable to bear the rage of the poison, he clawed at the ground until his fingernails were nearly gone, whereupon Liyong beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shuji was known to wear gold on his person. Liyong forced him to drink kudzu poison by the sheng. When he still would not die, the poison's fury drove him to rake the earth until his nails were nearly torn away—whereupon Liyong beat him to death anyway.

sentences.zh: 利用還，擢拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Upon Liyong's return, he was promoted to Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyong returned, he was promoted to Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 薛季昶累貶儋州司馬。

translations.literal: Xue Jichang was repeatedly demoted, ultimately to Military Assistant of Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jichang was demoted again and again, until at last he was sent to Dan Prefecture as military assistant.

sentences.zh: 飲藥死。

translations.literal: He drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: There he drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 三思既殺五王，權傾人主，常言：「我不知代間何者謂之善人，何者謂之惡人；

translations.literal: After Wu Sansi had killed the Five Princes, his power overshadowed even the sovereign. He often said: "I do not know which people of this age are called good and which are called evil;
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu Sansi had destroyed the Five Princes, his power eclipsed even the throne. He liked to say: "I no longer know who in this world counts as good and who as evil;

sentences.zh: 但於我善者則為善人，於我惡者則為惡人耳。」

translations.literal: Those who are good to me are good people, and those who are bad to me are evil people, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: whoever is good to me is good, and whoever is bad to me is evil—that is all there is to it."

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書宗禁客、將作大匠宗晉卿、太府卿紀處訥、鴻臚卿甘元柬皆為三思羽翼。

translations.literal: At this time, Minister of War Zong Chuke, Director of Palace Construction Zong Jinqing, Minister of the Grand Treasury Ji Chun'e, and Minister of Ceremonies Gan Yuanjian all served as Wu Sansi's wings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of War Zong Chuke, Director of Palace Construction Zong Jinqing, Minister of the Grand Treasury Ji Chun'e, and Minister of Ceremonies Gan Yuanjian all served as Wu Sansi's chief supporters.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞周利用、侍御史冉祖雍、太僕丞李俊、光祿丞宋之遜、監察御史姚紹之皆為三思耳目，時人謂之五狗。

translations.literal: Assistant Censor-in-Chief Zhou Liyong, Attending Censor Ran Zuyong, Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud Li Jun, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Song Zhixun, and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi all served as Wu Sansi's eyes and ears; contemporaries called them the Five Dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Censor-in-Chief Zhou Liyong, Attending Censor Ran Zuyong, Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud Li Jun, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Song Zhixun, and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi served as his eyes and ears in the bureaucracy. People of the day called them the Five Dogs.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，左散騎常侍、同中書門下三品李懷遠薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuwu, Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Secretariat-Chancellery Third-Rank Minister Li Huaiyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day wuwu, Li Huaiyuan—Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and a third-rank minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery—died.

sentences.zh: 初，李嶠為吏部侍郎，欲樹私恩，再求入相，奏大置員外官，廣引貴勢親識。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Qiao served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, wishing to cultivate private favor and seeking again to enter the Chancellery, he memorialized to greatly increase the number of supernumerary offices and broadly recruit powerful figures and personal acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as Vice Minister of Personnel, Li Qiao had sought to curry private favor and win his way back into the Chancellery. He memorialized for a vast expansion of supernumerary posts and filled them with powerful patrons and personal connections.

sentences.zh: 既而為相，銓衡失序，府庫減耗，乃更表言濫官之弊，且請遜位；

translations.literal: After he became Chancellor, the evaluation of officials fell into disorder and the treasury was depleted. He thereupon submitted another memorial on the evils of excessive appointments and requested to resign from his position;
translations.idiomatic: Once he had become Chancellor, the evaluation of officials collapsed into chaos and the treasury drained away. He then submitted another memorial lamenting the plague of excessive appointments and asked to step down;

sentences.zh: 上慰諭不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and instructed him, and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong comforted him and refused to accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，車駕發東都，以前檢校并州長史張仁願檢校左屯衛大將軍兼洛州長史。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jimao, the imperial carriage departed from the Eastern Capital. Former Acting Governor of Bingzhou Zhang Renyuan was appointed Acting General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard and concurrently Prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jimao, the imperial procession left Luoyang. Zhang Renyuan, formerly acting governor of Bingzhou, was appointed acting General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard and concurrently prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕至西京。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, the imperial carriage arrived at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu the imperial procession reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day yisi, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day yisi, a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以蒲州刺史竇從一為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Dou Congyi, Governor of Pu Prefecture, was appointed Governor of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Dou Congyi, governor of Pu Prefecture, was appointed governor of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從一，德玄之子也，初名懷貞，避皇后父諱，更名從一，多諂附權貴。

translations.literal: Congyi was the son of De Xuan. His original name was Huaizhen; to avoid the taboo name of the Empress's father, he changed it to Congyi. He was much given to flattering and attaching himself to the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was the son of De Xuan. He had originally been named Huaizhen, but changed his name to avoid the taboo on the Empress's father's name. He was notorious for fawning on the powerful.

sentences.zh: 太平公主與僧寺爭碾磑，雍州司戶李元紘判歸僧寺。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping disputed a water mill with a Buddhist monastery. Li Yuanhong, Registrar of Yong Prefecture, ruled in favor of the monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping quarreled with a Buddhist monastery over a water-powered mill. Li Yuanhong, registrar of Yong Prefecture, ruled in the monastery's favor.

sentences.zh: 從一大懼，亟命元紘改判。

translations.literal: Congyi was greatly alarmed and urgently ordered Yuanhong to reverse the judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was terrified and immediately ordered Yuanhong to reverse the ruling.

sentences.zh: 元紘大署判後曰：「南山可移，此判無動！」

translations.literal: Yuanhong wrote in large characters at the end of the judgment: "The South Mountain may be moved, but this ruling shall not be altered!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong wrote in bold characters at the foot of the judgment: "The South Mountain itself may be moved, but this ruling shall not!"

sentences.zh: 從一不能奪。

translations.literal: End of speech. Congyi could not overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Congyi could not budge him.

sentences.zh: 元紘，道廣之子也。

translations.literal: Yuanhong was the son of Dao Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong was the son of Dao Guang.

sentences.zh: 初，秘書監鄭普思納其女於後宮，監察御史靈昌崔日用劾奏之，上不聽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Director of the Secretariat Directorate Zheng Pusi had presented his daughter to the inner palace. Investigating Censor Cui Riyong of Lingchang impeached him, but the Emperor would not hear it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zheng Pusi, Director of the Secretariat Directorate, had offered his daughter to the inner palace. Investigating Censor Cui Riyong of Lingchang impeached him, but Zhongzong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 普思聚黨於雍、岐二州，謀作亂。

translations.literal: Pusi gathered a faction in Yong and Qi prefectures and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi gathered followers in Yong and Qi prefectures and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事覺，西京留守蘇瑰收系，窮治之。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Western Capital Defender Su Gui arrested and imprisoned him and investigated thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, Su Gui, Defender of Chang'an, arrested him and pursued the case to the end.

sentences.zh: 普思妻第五氏以鬼道得幸於皇后，上敕瑰勿治。

translations.literal: Pusi's wife, Lady Fifth, had gained favor with the Empress through sorcery. The Emperor ordered Su Gui not to pursue the case.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi's wife, Lady Fifth, had won Empress Wei's favor through dark arts. Zhongzong ordered Su Gui to drop the case.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還西京，瑰廷爭之，上抑瑰而佑普思；

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the Western Capital, Su Gui disputed the matter at court; the Emperor suppressed Su Gui and protected Pusi;
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned to Chang'an, Su Gui argued the matter fiercely at court. Zhongzong silenced Su Gui and shielded Pusi;

sentences.zh: 侍御史范獻忠進曰：「請斬蘇瑰！」

translations.literal: Attending Censor Fan Xianzhong stepped forward and said: "I request that Su Gui be executed!"
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Fan Xianzhong stepped forward and said: "I ask that Su Gui be executed!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: End of speech. The Emperor said: "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong asked: "On what grounds?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「瑰為留守大臣，不能先斬普思，然後奏聞，使之熒惑聖聽，其罪大矣。

translations.literal: End of speech. He replied: "As Defender, a great minister of the capital, Su Gui failed to execute Pusi first and then report to the throne, allowing him instead to deceive the Emperor's judgment. His offense is grave.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Fan replied: "As Defender—a chief minister of the capital—Su Gui should have executed Pusi first and reported afterward. Instead he let a traitor cloud the Emperor's ears. That is a grave crime.

sentences.zh: 且普思反狀明白，而陛下曲為申理。

translations.literal: Moreover, Pusi's treasonous conduct is clear, yet Your Majesty bends the law to exonerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi's rebellion is plain for all to see, yet Your Majesty twists the law to absolve him.

sentences.zh: 臣聞王者不死，殆謂是乎！

translations.literal: I have heard that a sovereign cannot be killed—perhaps this is what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that kings cannot be killed—perhaps this is what that means!

sentences.zh: 臣願先賜死，不能北面事普思。」

translations.literal: I would rather receive death first than serve Pusi with my face to the north."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me death first—I cannot bow north and serve Pusi."

sentences.zh: 魏元忠曰：「蘇瑰長者，用刑不枉。

translations.literal: End of speech. Wei Yuanzhong said: "Su Gui is a man of integrity; he does not misapply punishment.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Wei Yuanzhong said: "Su Gui is an upright man. He does not punish the innocent.

sentences.zh: 普思法當死。」

translations.literal: By law, Pusi ought to die."
translations.idiomatic: By law, Pusi deserves death."

sentences.zh: 上不得已，戊午，流普思於儋州，餘黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: End of speech. The Emperor, having no choice, on the day wuwu exiled Pusi to Dan Prefecture; the remaining conspirators were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Cornered, Zhongzong on the day wuwu exiled Pusi to Dan Prefecture. The rest of the conspirators were put to death.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己卯，突厥默啜寇鳴沙，靈武軍大總管沙吒忠義與戰，軍敗，死者六千餘人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jimao, the Türk Mo-ch'o raided Mingsha. Grand General of the Lingwu Army Sha Tuo Zhongyi fought him and was defeated; more than six thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day jimao, the Türk khan Mo-ch'o attacked Mingsha. Sha Tuo Zhongyi, Grand General of the Lingwu Army, met him in battle and was routed. More than six thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，突厥進寇原、會等州，掠隴右牧馬萬餘匹而去。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, the Türks advanced to raid Yuan, Hui, and other prefectures, plundered more than ten thousand horses from the Longyou pastures, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi the Türks pushed deeper, raiding Yuan, Hui, and neighboring prefectures. They drove off more than ten thousand horses from the Longyou pastures and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 免忠義官。

translations.literal: Zhongyi was stripped of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 安西大都護郭元振詣突騎施烏質勒牙帳議軍事，天大風雪，元振立於帳前，與烏質勒語。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Anxi Guo Yuanzhen went to the yurt of the Turgesh chieftain Wuzhile to discuss military affairs. A great wind and snowstorm arose. Yuanzhen stood before the tent and spoke with Wuzhile.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanzhen, Protector-General of Anxi, went to the yurt of the Turgesh chieftain Wuzhile to discuss military affairs. A fierce blizzard blew up, yet Yuanzhen stood before the tent and spoke with him face to face.

sentences.zh: 久之，雪深，元振不移足；

translations.literal: After a long while the snow grew deep, yet Yuanzhen did not shift his feet;
translations.idiomatic: A long while passed and the snow piled deep, but Yuanzhen never moved his feet;

sentences.zh: 烏質勒老，不勝寒，會罷而卒。

translations.literal: Wuzhile was old and could not endure the cold; when the meeting ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile was old and could not withstand the cold. When the meeting ended, he died.

sentences.zh: 其子娑葛勒兵將攻元振，副使御之中丞解琬知之，勸元振夜逃去。

translations.literal: His son Suoge gathered troops intending to attack Yuanzhen. Vice-commissioner and Imperial Censor-in-Chief Xie Wan learned of this and urged Yuanzhen to flee by night.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suoge mustered troops to attack Yuanzhen. Xie Wan, the vice-commissioner and Imperial Censor-in-Chief, learned of it and urged Yuanzhen to flee under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「吾以誠心待人，何所疑懼！

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "I treat others with sincere intent—what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said: "I have dealt with others in good faith—what is there to fear!

sentences.zh: 且深在寇庭，逃將安適！」

translations.literal: Moreover, deep in the enemy camp, where would flight lead?"
translations.idiomatic: And deep in the enemy camp, where would flight even take me?"

sentences.zh: 安臥不動。

translations.literal: End of speech. He lay down peacefully and did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. He lay down calmly and did not move.

sentences.zh: 明旦，入哭，甚哀。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he entered to mourn, weeping with great grief.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day he went in to mourn, weeping with deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 娑葛感其義，待元振如初。

translations.literal: Suoge was moved by his righteousness and treated Yuanzhen as before.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge was moved by his integrity and treated Yuanzhen exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以娑葛襲嗢鹿州都督、懷德王。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Suoge succeeded to the posts of Protector of Wulu Prefecture and Prince of Huaide.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Suoge succeeded to the posts of Protector of Wulu Prefecture and Prince of Huaide.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主恃寵驕恣，賣官鬻獄，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Princess Anle, relying on imperial favor, grew arrogant and unrestrained, selling offices and trafficking in judicial verdicts until her power overshadowed court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle, drunk on imperial favor, grew arrogant and unchecked. She sold offices and bought verdicts until her power dwarfed everyone at court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 或自為制敕，掩其文，令上署之；

translations.literal: Sometimes she herself drafted imperial edicts, covered over the text, and had the Emperor sign them;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes she drafted edicts herself, hid the text, and had Zhongzong sign them;

sentences.zh: 上笑而從之，竟不視也。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and complied, never even looking at what he signed.
translations.idiomatic: He would smile and oblige, never once bothering to read what he had signed.

sentences.zh: 自請為皇太女，上雖不從，亦不譴責。

translations.literal: She requested to be made Imperial Crown Princess; though the Emperor did not consent, he also did not reprove her.
translations.idiomatic: She even asked to be made Imperial Crown Princess. Zhongzong refused, but did not rebuke her.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚戌，制以突厥默啜寇邊，命內外官各進平突厥之策。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day gengxu, an edict was issued because the Türk Mo-ch'o was raiding the frontier, ordering officials within and without the court each to submit plans for pacifying the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the day gengxu, an edict was issued: because the Türk khan Mo-ch'o was raiding the frontier, every official inside and outside the court was to submit a plan for pacifying the Türks.

sentences.zh: 右補闕盧輔上疏，以為：「郤谷悅禮樂，敦詩書，為晉元帥；

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Lu Fu submitted a memorial arguing: "Xi Gu delighted in ritual and music and devoted himself to the Odes and Documents, yet served as Jin's commander-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Officer Lu Fu submitted a memorial arguing: "Xi Gu loved ritual and music and steeped himself in the Odes and Documents, yet he commanded Jin's armies;

sentences.zh: 杜預射不穿禮，建平吳之勳。

translations.literal: Du Yu could not pierce a target with an arrow but established the merit of pacifying Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu was no archer, yet he won the merit of pacifying Wu.

sentences.zh: 是知中權制謀，不取一夫之勇。

translations.literal: This shows that central authority plans strategy and does not rely on the bravery of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that strategy belongs to those who hold central authority—not to the lone warrior's courage.

sentences.zh: 如沙吒忠義，驍將之材，本不足以當大任。

translations.literal: Someone like Sha Tuo Zhongyi, though possessing the talent of a fierce general, is fundamentally unfit for a great command.
translations.idiomatic: A man like Sha Tuo Zhongyi may have the makings of a fierce general, but he is not fit for supreme command.

sentences.zh: 又，鳴沙之役，主將先逃，宜正邦憲；

translations.literal: Further, in the battle of Mingsha the commander fled first; he should be punished according to the laws of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at Mingsha the commander fled before his men. He should be punished under the laws of the realm;

sentences.zh: 賞罰既明，敵無不服。

translations.literal: When rewards and punishments are clear, no enemy will fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: when reward and punishment are clear, no enemy will refuse to submit.

sentences.zh: 又，邊州刺史，宜精擇其人，使之蒐卒乘，積資糧，來則御史，去則備之。

translations.literal: Further, frontier prefects should be carefully chosen, so that they may gather troops and chariots, stockpile provisions, and strike the enemy when they come and prepare defenses when they depart.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier prefects, too, must be chosen with care, so they can muster troops, stockpile grain, strike when the enemy comes, and fortify when they leave.

sentences.zh: 去歲四方旱災，未易興師。

translations.literal: Last year drought struck all quarters of the realm; it is not easy to raise an army now.
translations.idiomatic: Last year drought ravaged the empire. This is no time to raise a great army.

sentences.zh: 當理內以及外，綏近以來遠，俟倉廩實，士卒練，然後大舉以討之。」

translations.literal: One ought to put the interior in order before reaching outward, pacify those nearby to win those far away, wait until granaries are full and soldiers well trained, and only then launch a major campaign to subdue them."
translations.idiomatic: Put the interior in order before looking outward; win those nearby before drawing in those far away. Wait until the granaries are full and the soldiers trained—only then launch the great campaign to crush them."

sentences.zh: 上善之。

translations.literal: End of speech. The Emperor approved his views.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，上遣武攸暨、武三思詣乾陵祈雨。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day bingxu, the Emperor sent Wu Youji and Wu Sansi to Qianling to pray for rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingxu, Zhongzong sent Wu Youji and Wu Sansi to Qianling to pray for rain.

sentences.zh: 既而雨降，上喜，制復武氏崇恩廟及昊陵、順陵，因名酆王廟曰褒德，陵曰榮先；

translations.literal: Rain soon fell. The Emperor was pleased and issued an edict restoring the Wu clan's Chong'en Temple as well as Haoling and Shunling. Accordingly he renamed the Prince of Feng's temple as Baode and his tomb as Rongxian;
translations.idiomatic: Rain soon fell. Delighted, Zhongzong issued an edict restoring the Wu clan's Chong'en Temple along with Haoling and Shunling. He renamed the Prince of Feng's temple Baode and his tomb Rongxian;

sentences.zh: 又制崇恩廟齋郎取五品子充。

translations.literal: Another edict provided that temple attendants of Chong'en Temple were to be drawn from sons of fifth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: another edict stipulated that Chong'en Temple's ritual attendants were to be drawn from sons of fifth-rank officials.

sentences.zh: 太常博士楊孚曰：「太廟皆取七品已下子為齋郎，今崇恩廟取五品子，未知太廟當如何？」

translations.literal: Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yang Fu said: "The Imperial Ancestral Temple always takes sons of seventh rank and below as temple attendants. Now Chong'en Temple takes sons of fifth rank—what is the Imperial Ancestral Temple to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, objected: "The Imperial Ancestral Temple has always drawn its ritual attendants from sons of seventh rank and below. If Chong'en Temple now takes sons of fifth rank, what becomes of the Imperial Ancestral Temple?"

sentences.zh: 上命太廟亦准崇恩廟。

translations.literal: End of speech. The Emperor ordered the Imperial Ancestral Temple to follow Chong'en Temple's standard as well.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong ordered the Imperial Ancestral Temple to follow Chong'en Temple's standard.

sentences.zh: 孚曰：「以臣准君，猶為僭逆，況以君准臣乎！」

translations.literal: Yang Fu said: "Using a subject as the standard for a lord is already usurpation and treason—how much more so using a lord as standard for a subject!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu said: "To measure a lord by a subject is already usurpation—how much worse to measure a lord's temple by a subject's!"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: End of speech. The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong relented.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，敕改諸州中興寺、觀為龍興，自今奏事不得言中興。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, an edict ordered that Zhongxing temples and monasteries in all prefectures be renamed Longxing; from this day forward memorials were not to use the word zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, an edict renamed every Zhongxing temple and monastery in the realm to Longxing. Henceforth memorials were forbidden to use the word "Restoration."

sentences.zh: 右補闕權若訥上疏，以為：「天、地、日、月等字皆則天能事，賊臣敬暉等輕紊前規；

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Quan Ruonuo submitted a memorial arguing: "Characters such as Heaven, Earth, Sun, and Moon were all feats of Empress Zetian. The traitorous ministers Jing Hui and others recklessly disturbed these earlier regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Officer Quan Ruonuo submitted a memorial arguing: "The characters for Heaven, Earth, Sun, and Moon were all innovations of Empress Zetian. Traitors like Jing Hui rashly overturned those precedents;

sentences.zh: 今削之無益於淳化，存之有光於孝理。

translations.literal: To remove them now would not aid in purifying customs, while preserving them would honor filial principle.
translations.idiomatic: to erase them now would not purify the age, but to preserve them would honor filial duty.

sentences.zh: 又，神龍元年制書，一事以上，並依貞觀故事，豈可近捨母儀，遠尊祖德！」

translations.literal: Further, the Shenlong first-year edict stipulated that in all matters one should follow the precedents of the Zhenguan era—how can one discard the model of one's mother nearby yet honor ancestral virtue from afar!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Shenlong edict of the first year declared that all affairs should follow Zhenguan precedent. How can we abandon our mother's example while claiming to honor our ancestors from afar!"

sentences.zh: 疏奏，手制褒美。

translations.literal: End of speech. When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor personally drafted an edict praising it.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. When the memorial arrived, Zhongzong personally drafted an edict commending it.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚子，吐蕃遣其大臣悉薰熱入貢。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day gengzi, Tibet sent its minister Xixinre to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day gengzi, Tibet sent its minister Xixinre to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，以上所養雍王守禮女金城公主妻吐蕃贊普。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinsi, the Emperor gave in marriage to the Tibetan tsenpo the Princess Jincheng, daughter of Yong Wang Shouli whom he had raised.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the day xinsi, Zhongzong gave Princess Jincheng—daughter of Yong Wang Shouli, whom he had raised as his own—in marriage to the Tibetan tsenpo.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊戌，以右屯衛大將軍張仁願為朔方道大總管，以備突厥。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day wuxu, General-in-Chief of the Right Garrison Guard Zhang Renyuan was appointed Grand General of the Shuofang Circuit to guard against the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wuxu, Zhang Renyuan, General-in-Chief of the Right Garrison Guard, was appointed Grand General of the Shuofang Circuit to guard against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 上以歲旱谷貴，召太府卿紀處訥謀之。

translations.literal: Because of drought and the high price of grain, the Emperor summoned Minister of the Grand Treasury Ji Chun'e to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: With drought driving up grain prices, Zhongzong summoned Ji Chun'e, Minister of the Grand Treasury, to discuss what could be done.

sentences.zh: 明日，武三思使知太史事迦葉志忠奏：「是夜，攝提入太微宮，至帝座，主大臣宴見納忠於天子。」

translations.literal: The next day, Wu Sansi had Yeji Zhizhong, who oversaw the Directorate of Astronomy, report: "That night Zhijie entered the Taiwei Palace and reached the Emperor's throne, signifying that a great minister would be received in audience and loyalty would be welcomed by the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wu Sansi had Yeji Zhizhong, overseer of the Directorate of Astronomy, report: "That very night Zhijie entered the Taiwei Palace and reached the Emperor's throne—a sign that a great minister would be received in audience and loyalty welcomed at court."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，敕稱處訥忠誠，徹於玄象，賜衣一襲，帛六十段。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right and issued an edict praising Chunna's loyalty, manifest in the celestial signs, granting him one suit of robes and sixty lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong agreed and issued an edict praising Chunna's loyalty as written in the heavens, granting him one suit of robes and sixty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day dingmao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day dingmao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 姚巂道討擊使、監察御史晉昌唐九征擊姚州叛蠻，破之，斬獲三千餘人。

translations.literal: The punitive commissioner of the Yao–Xi route and censor Tang Jiuzheng of Jinchang attacked the rebel barbarians of Yao Prefecture, defeated them, and killed or captured more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiuzheng, punitive commissioner on the Yao–Xi route and censor from Jinchang, struck the rebellious tribes of Yao Prefecture, routed them, and killed or captured over three thousand.

sentences.zh: 皇后以太子重俊非其所生，惡之；

translations.literal: Because Crown Prince Chongjun was not born of her, the empress hated him;
translations.idiomatic: The empress loathed Crown Prince Chongjun, for he was not her own son;

sentences.zh: 特進德靜王武三思尤忌太子。

translations.literal: The specially advanced Prince Dejing, Wu Sansi, especially resented the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, Prince Dejing and holder of special advancement, above all feared and envied the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上官婕妤以三思故，每下制敕，推尊武氏。

translations.literal: Consort Shangguan, on account of Sansi, whenever issuing edicts, exalted the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Because of her tie to Sansi, Consort Shangguan used every edict she drafted to elevate the Wu family.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主與駙馬左衛將軍武崇訓常陵侮太子，或呼為奴。

translations.literal: Princess Anle and her consort, Left Guard General Wu Chongxun, often insulted and humiliated the crown prince, sometimes calling him a slave.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle and her husband Wu Chongxun, Left Guard General, routinely belittled the crown prince—at times they even called him a bondservant.

sentences.zh: 崇訓又教公主言於上，請廢太子，立己為皇太女。

translations.literal: Chongxun also instructed the princess to speak to the emperor, requesting that the crown prince be deposed and that she herself be established as heir apparent princess.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun further coached the princess to petition Zhongzong to remove the crown prince and name her heir to the throne—the unprecedented rank of crown princess.

sentences.zh: 太子積不能平。

translations.literal: The crown prince accumulated grievances and could not remain at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Grievance piled upon grievance until the crown prince could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛丑，太子與左羽林大將軍李多祚、將軍李思沖、李承況、獨孤禕之、沙吒忠義等，矯制發羽林千騎兵三百餘人，殺三思、崇訓於其第，並親黨十餘人。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinchou, the crown prince, together with Left Forest General Li Duozuo and the generals Li Sichong, Li Chengkang, Dugu Yizhi, Shazha Zhongyi, and others, forged an edict and mobilized more than three hundred soldiers of the Left Forest Thousand Riders, killing Sansi and Chongxun at their residences, along with more than ten of their close partisans.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinchou day, Crown Prince Chongjun, Li Duozuo the Left Forest General, and the generals Li Sichong, Li Chengkang, Dugu Yizhi, and Shazha Zhongyi forged an imperial order and led three hundred-odd Left Forest cavalry to storm the mansions of Sansi and Chongxun, killing them and more than ten of their intimates.

sentences.zh: 又使左金吾大將軍成王千里及其子天水王禧分兵守宮城諸門，太子與多祚引兵自肅章門斬關而入，叩閣索上官婕妤。

translations.literal: He also sent Left Golden Guard General Prince Cheng of Qianli and his son Prince Tian of Xi to divide their forces and hold the various gates of the palace city; the crown prince and Duozuo led troops through the SuZhang Gate, cutting the barrier to enter, and knocked at the inner gate demanding Consort Shangguan.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Prince Cheng of Qianli, Left Golden Guard General, and his son Prince Tian of Xi to seize the palace gates, while he and Duozuo broke through SuZhang Gate and battered at the inner doors, demanding Consort Shangguan be handed over.

sentences.zh: 婕妤大言曰：「觀其意欲先索婉兒，次索皇后，次及大家。」

translations.literal: The consort cried out loudly, saying: "Judging by their intent, they wish first to seize Wan'er, next to seize the empress, and next to reach His Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shangguan shouted for all to hear: "Mark their aim—they mean first to take me, Wan'er; next the empress; and after that, the Emperor himself."

sentences.zh: 上乃與韋後、安樂公主、上官婕妤登玄武門樓以避兵鋒，使左羽林大將軍劉景仁帥飛騎百餘人屯於樓下以自衛。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor then, together with Empress Wei, Princess Anle, and Consort Shangguan, ascended the tower of Xuanyuan Gate to avoid the edge of the soldiers' blades, and sent Left Forest General Liu Jingren to command more than a hundred flying cavalry to encamp below the tower for his own protection.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong then climbed the Xuanyuan Gate tower with Empress Wei, Princess Anle, and Consort Shangguan to escape the fighting, while Liu Jingren, Left Forest General, posted a hundred flying cavalry below to guard them.

sentences.zh: 楊再思、蘇瑰、李嶠與兵部尚書宗楚客、左衛將軍紀處訥擁兵二千餘人屯太極殿前，閉門自守。

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi, Su Gui, and Li Jiao, together with Minister of War Zong Chuke and Left Guard General Ji Chune, mustered more than two thousand troops and encamped before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, closing the gates to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi, Su Gui, and Li Jiao joined Minister of War Zong Chuke and Left Guard General Ji Chune in rallying over two thousand men before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, barricading the doors.

sentences.zh: 多祚先至玄武樓下，欲升樓，宿衛拒之。

translations.literal: Duozuo arrived first below the Xuanyuan tower, wished to ascend, and the palace guards refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo reached the foot of the Xuanyuan tower first and tried to climb up, but the palace guards turned him back.

sentences.zh: 多祚與太子狐疑，按兵不戰，冀上問之。

translations.literal: Duozuo and the crown prince hesitated in doubt, held their troops and did not fight, hoping the emperor would summon them.
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo and the crown prince wavered, holding their men idle in the hope that Zhongzong would call them to audience.

sentences.zh: 宮闈令石城楊思勖在上側，請擊之。

translations.literal: Palace Aide Yang Sinu of Shicheng, at the emperor's side, requested permission to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sinu, palace aide of Shicheng, standing at Zhongzong's side, begged leave to strike.

sentences.zh: 多祚婿羽林中郎將野呼利為前鋒總管，思勖挺刃斬之，多祚軍奪氣。

translations.literal: Duozuo's son-in-law, Forest Guard Captain Yehuli, served as vanguard commander; Sinu drew his blade and beheaded him, and Duozuo's army lost its fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yehuli, Duozuo's son-in-law and vanguard commander of the Forest Guard, fell when Sinu stepped forward and cut off his head; Duozuo's force lost heart at once.

sentences.zh: 上據檻俯謂多祚所將千騎曰：「汝輩皆朕宿衛之士，何為從多祚反？

translations.literal: The emperor leaned on the railing and looked down, saying to the thousand riders led by Duozuo: "You are all my personal guard soldiers—why follow Duozuo in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong leaned over the balustrade and called down to Duozuo's thousand riders: "Every one of you is sworn to guard my person—why do you follow Duozuo in treason?

sentences.zh: 苟能斬反者，勿患不富貴。」

translations.literal: If you can behead the rebels, do not worry that you will not be enriched and ennobled."
translations.idiomatic: Slay the rebels, and wealth and rank will be yours—have no fear of that."

sentences.zh: 於是千騎斬多祚、承況、禕之、忠義，餘眾皆潰。

translations.literal: End of speech. Thereupon the thousand riders beheaded Duozuo, Chengkang, Yizhi, and Zhongyi, and the remaining multitude all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. At once the thousand riders cut down Duozuo, Chengkang, Yizhi, and Zhongyi; the rest broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 成王千里、天水王禧攻右延明門，將殺宗楚客、紀處訥，不克而死。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Qianli and Prince Tian of Xi attacked the Right Gate of Extended Brightness, intending to kill Zong Chuke and Ji Chune; they did not succeed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Qianli and Prince Tian of Xi assaulted the Right Gate of Extended Brightness to kill Zong Chuke and Ji Chune; failing, they were slain in turn.

sentences.zh: 太子以百騎走終南山，至鄠西，能屬者才數人，憩於林下，為左右所殺。

translations.literal: The crown prince fled with a hundred riders to Mount Zhongnan, reaching the west of E; those who could follow him numbered only a few. Resting beneath the trees, he was killed by his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince galloped toward Mount Zhongnan with a hundred horsemen, but by the time he reached western E only a handful remained. He paused under the trees—and his own followers killed him.

sentences.zh: 上以其首獻太廟及祭三思、崇訓之柩，然後梟之朝堂。

translations.literal: The emperor offered his head to the ancestral temple and before the coffins at the mourning rites for Sansi and Chongxun, and only then displayed it at the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong first presented the head at the ancestral temple and before the biers of Sansi and Chongxun; only then was it hung in the court hall for all to see.

sentences.zh: 更成王千里姓曰蝮氏，同黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: He changed Prince Cheng of Qianli's surname to the clan of the viper; all co-conspirators were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Qianli's clan name was changed to Viper; every accomplice was put to death.

sentences.zh: 東宮僚屬無敢近太子屍者，唯永和縣丞寧嘉勖解衣裹太子首號哭，貶興平丞。

translations.literal: None of the Eastern Palace staff dared approach the crown prince's corpse; only Ning Jiaxu, assistant magistrate of Yonghe County, removed his garment to wrap the crown prince's head and wailed aloud. He was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Not one official of the Eastern Palace would go near the prince's body. Only Ning Jiaxu, assistant magistrate of Yonghe, stripped off his own robe to wrap the severed head and wept openly—for which he was banished to a post in Xingping.

sentences.zh: 太子兵所經諸門守者皆坐流；

translations.literal: The keepers of every gate through which the crown prince's troops had passed were all sentenced to exile;
translations.idiomatic: Every gatekeeper along the crown prince's route was sentenced to exile;

sentences.zh: 韋氏之黨奏請悉誅之，上更命法司推斷。

translations.literal: the faction of the Wei clan memorialized requesting that all be executed; the emperor again ordered the judicial offices to review the case.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei faction petitioned that they all be executed, but Zhongzong sent the case back for judicial review.

sentences.zh: 大理卿宋城鄭惟忠曰：「大獄始決，人心未安，若復有改推，則反仄者眾矣。」

translations.literal: Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Weizhong of Songcheng said: "This great case has only just been decided and the people's hearts are not yet settled; if there is another revision of judgment, then those unsettled will be many."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weizhong, chief justice of the Court of Judicial Review, argued: "The verdict in this grave matter is fresh, and the realm is still unsettled. Reopen the inquiry, and unrest will spread far and wide."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong relented.

sentences.zh: 以楊思勖為銀青光祿大夫，行內常侍。

translations.literal: Yang Sinu was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Attendance and acting Inner Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sinu was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Attendance and acting Inner Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day, Zhongzong proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 贈武三思太尉、梁宣王，武崇訓開府儀同三司、魯忠王。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi was posthumously honored as Grand Commander and Prince Xuan of Liang; Wu Chongxun as Grand Master of the Palace with the same ceremonial precedence as the Three Excellencies and Prince Zhong of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors fell upon Wu Sansi as Grand Commander and Prince Xuan of Liang, and upon Wu Chongxun as a palace-grade minister of the first rank and Prince Zhong of Lu.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主請用永泰公主故事，以崇訓墓為陵。

translations.literal: Princess Anle requested that the precedent of Princess Yongtai be applied, making Chongxun's tomb a mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle asked that Chongxun's grave be elevated to a mausoleum, as had been done for Princess Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧粲駁之，以為：「永泰事出特恩，今魯王主婿，不可為比。」

translations.literal: Attendant Lu Can rebutted it, stating: "The matter of Yongtai arose from a special grace; now the Prince of Lu is the emperor's son-in-law and cannot be compared."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Lu Can objected: "Princess Yongtai's case was a singular act of imperial favor. The Prince of Lu is the emperor's son-in-law—the two cannot be equated."

sentences.zh: 上手敕曰：「安樂與永泰無異，同穴之義，今古不殊。」

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor's handwritten edict said: "Anle and Yongtai are no different; the principle of sharing one tomb is the same in ancient times and today."
translations.idiomatic: End of edict. Zhongzong wrote back in his own hand: "Anle and Yongtai are alike in this—husband and wife buried together is a bond honored in every age."

sentences.zh: 粲又奏，以為：「陛下以膝下之愛施及其夫，豈可使上下無辨，君臣一貫哉！」

translations.literal: End of edict. Lu Can again memorialized, stating: "Your Majesty extends the love beneath your knee to their husbands—how can you make superior and inferior undistinguished and lord and minister of one piece!"
translations.idiomatic: End of edict. Lu Can pressed on: "Your Majesty pours a father's tenderness upon their husbands as well—will you blur the line between sovereign and subject, prince and minister, until none can tell them apart?"

sentences.zh: 上乃從之。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor then yielded to him.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. At last Zhongzong conceded.

sentences.zh: 公主怒，出粲為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: The princess grew angry and had Lu Can sent out as prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, furious, had Lu Can packed off to serve as prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 襄邑尉襄陽席豫聞安樂公主求為太女，歎曰：「梅福譏切王氏，獨何人哉！」

translations.literal: Xiangyi magistrate Xi Yu of Xiangyang, hearing that Princess Anle sought to become heir apparent princess, sighed and said: "Mei Fu satirized the Wang clan with biting words—what sort of man am I!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Yu of Xiangyang, magistrate of Xiangyi, learned that Princess Anle was pressing to be named crown princess, he sighed: "Mei Fu once scourged the Wang usurpation with his pen—what am I, that I should stay silent?"

sentences.zh: 乃上書請立太子，言甚深切。

translations.literal: End of speech. He then submitted a memorial requesting that the crown prince be established; his words were very earnest and deep.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. He memorialized the throne, pleading that the legitimate heir be upheld; his words cut to the bone.

sentences.zh: 太平公主欲表為諫官。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping wished to memorialize recommending him as a remonstrating official.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping meant to nominate him for a remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 豫恥之，逃去。

translations.literal: Yu was ashamed of this and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, Xi Yu slipped away and vanished.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊寅，皇后及王公已下表上尊號曰應天神龍皇帝，改玄武門為神武門，樓為制勝樓。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuyin, the empress and the princes and dukes down submitted a memorial offering the honorific title Responding Heaven, Divine Dragon Emperor; Xuanyuan Gate was renamed Divine Martial Gate, and its tower was renamed Tower of Decisive Victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuyin day, Empress Wei and the princes and nobles below petitioned that Zhongzong take the title Responding Heaven, Divine Dragon Emperor; Xuanyuan Gate became Divine Martial Gate, its tower the Tower of Decisive Victory.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客又帥百官表請加皇后尊號曰順天翊聖皇后。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke again led the hundred officials in a memorial requesting that an honorific be added for the empress: Compliant Heaven, Assisting Sage Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke rallied the bureaucracy to ask that the empress receive the added title Compliant Heaven, Assisting Sage Empress.

sentences.zh: 上並許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted both.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong approved both petitions.

sentences.zh: 初，右台大夫蘇珦治太子重俊之黨，囚有引相王者，珦密為之申理，上乃不問。

translations.literal: Initially, when Right Censor-in-Chief Su Xian investigated the faction of Crown Prince Chongjun, prisoners implicated the Prince of Xiang; Xian secretly vindicated him, and the emperor then did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Right Censor-in-Chief Su Xian first investigated Crown Prince Chongjun's accomplices, some prisoners named the Prince of Xiang. Su quietly cleared him, and Zhongzong let the accusation drop.

sentences.zh: 自是安樂公主及兵部尚書宗楚客日夜謀譖相王，使侍御史冉祖雍等誣奏相王及太平公主，云「與重俊通謀，請收付制獄。」

translations.literal: From this time Princess Anle and Minister of War Zong Chuke day and night plotted slander against the Prince of Xiang, sending Remonstrating Censor Ran Zuyong and others to lodge a false accusation against the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping, saying: "They colluded with Chongjun in conspiracy; please arrest them and commit them to the controlled prison."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Princess Anle and Minister of War Zong Chuke worked day and night to destroy the Prince of Xiang, dispatching Remonstrating Censor Ran Zuyong to accuse him and Princess Taiping of plotting with Chongjun and demanding they be clapped in the deepest dungeon.

sentences.zh: 上召吏部侍郎兼御史中丞蕭至忠，使鞫之。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor summoned Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Xiao Zhizhong and ordered him to examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong called in Xiao Zhizhong, vice minister of personnel and censor-in-chief, to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 至忠泣曰：「陛下富有四海，不能容一弟一妹，而使人羅織害之乎！

translations.literal: Zhizhong wept and said: "Your Majesty possesses all within the four seas—can you not tolerate one younger brother and one younger sister, yet allow men to weave accusations to harm them!
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong wept aloud: "Your Majesty holds the four seas in your hand—can you not find room for one brother and one sister, while others spin webs of false charge to destroy them?

sentences.zh: 相王昔為皇嗣，固請於則天，以天下讓陛下，累日不食，此海內所知。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang was once heir apparent and firmly petitioned Empress Zetian to yield the realm to Your Majesty, going many days without eating—this all within the seas know.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang was once crown prince himself. He begged Empress Wu to pass the throne to you and went days without food—the whole empire remembers.

sentences.zh: 奈何以祖雍一言而疑之！」

translations.literal: How can you suspect him on the basis of a single word from Zuyong!"
translations.idiomatic: How can one word from Ran Zuyong overturn a lifetime of loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 上素友愛，遂寢其事。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor had always been fraternal in affection, and so set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong, who had ever cherished his kin, let the matter die.

sentences.zh: 右補闕浚儀吳兢聞祖雍之謀，上疏，以為：『自文明以來，國之祚胤，不絕如線，陛下龍興，恩及九族，求之瘴海，升之闕庭。

translations.literal: Right Supplementation Remonstrator Wu Jing of Junyi, hearing of Zuyong's plot, submitted a memorial, stating: "Since the reign title Civilizing, the imperial line of succession has hung by a thread; Your Majesty rose like a dragon, extending grace to the nine kinship groups, seeking them even in malarial seas and raising them to the court of the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing of Junyi, Right Supplementation Remonstrator, learning of Ran Zuyong's scheme, submitted a memorial: "Since the Civilizing era the imperial bloodline has hung by a thread. When Your Majesty ascended, you showered grace on every branch of the clan—men sought in fever swamps and brought to stand before the throne."

sentences.zh: 況相王同氣至親，六合無貳，而賊臣日夜連謀，乃欲陷之極法；

translations.literal: "Moreover, the Prince of Xiang shares the same breath and is kin of the closest degree; within the six directions there is no second loyalty, yet villainous ministers plot day and night in concert, intending to entrap him with the utmost penalty;"
translations.idiomatic: "The Prince of Xiang is bone of Your Majesty's bone—there is no divided allegiance under Heaven. Yet scheming ministers conspire night and day to bring him to the executioner's block;"

sentences.zh: 禍亂之根，將由此始。

translations.literal: "the root of calamity and disorder will begin from this."
translations.idiomatic: "from such a beginning comes the root of every calamity yet to come."

sentences.zh: 夫任以權則雖疏必重，奪其勢則雖親必輕。

translations.literal: "When one is entrusted with power, though distant he must be held weighty; when one's position is stripped, though close he must be held light."
translations.idiomatic: "Grant a man power and even a stranger grows heavy in the scales; strip a kinsman of standing and even blood weighs light."

sentences.zh: 自古委信異姓，猜忌骨肉，以覆國亡家者，幾何人矣！
