translations.literal: "From antiquity, those who entrusted faith to men of other surnames and suspected their own flesh and bone, thereby overturning states and destroying families—how many have there been!"
translations.idiomatic: "Since antiquity, how many thrones have fallen because rulers trusted outsiders and doubted their own flesh!"

sentences.zh: 況國家枝葉無幾，陛下登極未久，而一子以弄兵受誅，一子以愆違遠竄，惟餘一弟朝夕左右，尺布斗粟之譏，不可不慎，《青蠅》之詩，良可畏也！」

translations.literal: "Moreover, the branches and leaves of the state are few; Your Majesty has ascended the throne not long, and already one son has been executed for wielding troops in rebellion, one son has fled far away for transgression, and only one younger brother remains at your side morning and evening. The reproach of 'a foot of cloth, a peck of grain' must not be treated lightly; the ode 'Blue Flies' is truly something to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: "The dynasty's branches are already thin. Your Majesty has reigned but a short while: one son dead for raising arms, another banished for fault, and only one brother left at your side day and night. Beware the old reproach of brothers who grudged cloth and grain; dread the poem that warns of flies buzzing slander into the king's ear!"

sentences.zh: 相王寬厚恭謹，安恬好讓，故經武、韋之世，竟免於難。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang was generous, thick, respectful, and cautious, calm and fond of yielding; therefore through the eras of Wu and Wei he ultimately escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang was mild, courteous, and self-effacing—traits that saw him safely through the reigns of the Wu and Wei factions when so many others perished.

sentences.zh: 初，右僕射、中書令魏元忠以武三思擅權，意常憤郁。

translations.literal: Initially, Right Vice Director and Palace Secretariat Director Wei Yuanzhong, because Wu Sansi monopolized power, was often aggrieved and depressed in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong, Right Vice Director and head of the Palace Secretariat, had long brooded over Wu Sansi's monopoly on power.

sentences.zh: 及太子重俊起兵，遇元忠子太僕少卿升於永安門，脅以自隨，太子死，升為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chongjun raised troops, he encountered Yuanzhong's son Sheng, Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, at Yong'an Gate and coerced him to follow; after the crown prince died, Sheng was killed by the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chongjun rose in arms, he seized Yuanzhong's son Sheng, vice minister of the Imperial Stud, at Yong'an Gate and forced him along. After the prince's death, the mutineers killed Sheng.

sentences.zh: 元忠揚言曰：「元惡已死，雖鼎鑊何傷！

translations.literal: Yuanzhong declared publicly: "The chief villain is already dead—even the cauldron and boiling cannot harm me!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong proclaimed openly: "The arch-villain is dead—let them boil me in a cauldron if they will!

sentences.zh: 但惜太子隕沒耳！」

translations.literal: I only regret that the crown prince has fallen and perished!"
translations.idiomatic: My only sorrow is that the crown prince is gone."

sentences.zh: 上以其有功，且為高宗、武後所重，故釋不問。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor, because he had merit and was moreover esteemed by Emperor Gaozong and Empress Wu, therefore released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong, weighing his past service and the esteem in which Gaozong and Empress Wu had held him, let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書宗楚客、太府卿紀處訥等共證元忠，云「與太子通謀，請夷其三族。」

translations.literal: Minister of War Zong Chuke, Minister of the Imperial Storehouse Ji Chune, and others jointly testified against Yuanzhong, saying: "He conspired with the crown prince; please exterminate his three clans."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zong Chuke, Minister of the Imperial Storehouse Ji Chune, and others testified that Yuanzhong had plotted with the crown prince and demanded his clan be wiped out to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 制不許。

translations.literal: End of speech. An edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: End of edict. Zhongzong refused.

sentences.zh: 元忠懼，表請解官爵，以散秩還第。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong grew afraid and submitted a memorial requesting to resign his offices and ranks, returning home with an honorary title.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing worse, Yuanzhong petitioned to surrender his offices and retire on a nominal rank.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，上手敕聽解僕射，以特進、齊公致仕，仍朝朔望。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, the emperor's handwritten edict granted him leave to resign as vice director, retiring with the specially advanced rank and as Duke of Qi, still attending court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day Zhongzong accepted his resignation as vice director, granting him special advancement and the title Duke of Qi in retirement, with permission to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯，以吏部侍郎蕭至忠為黃門侍郎，兵部尚書宗楚客為左衛將軍，兼太府卿紀處訥為太府卿，並同中書門下三品；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingmao, Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Zhizhong was appointed as Vice Director of the Palace Gate; Minister of War Zong Chuke as Left Guard General; Ji Chune, who concurrently served as Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, as Minister of the Imperial Storehouse—all with concurrent status as Associates of the Three Departments;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingmao day, Xiao Zhizhong moved from vice minister of personnel to vice director of the Palace Gate; Zong Chuke from minister of war to Left Guard General; Ji Chune was confirmed as minister of the Imperial Storehouse—all three raised to associate rank in the Three Departments;

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同中書門下三品-{于}-惟謙罷為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate of the Three Departments Yu Weiqian was dismissed and made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weiqian, vice director of the Palace Secretariat and associate of the Three Departments, was removed and made chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 庚子，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Zhongzong proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客等引右衛郎將姚廷筠為御史中丞，使劾奏魏元忠，以為：「侯君集社稷元勳，及其謀反，太宗就群臣乞其命而不得，竟流涕斬之。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke and others brought in Right Guard Captain Yao Tingyun as Censor-in-Chief and had him impeach Wei Yuanzhong, stating: "Hou Junji was a founding minister of the altars of soil and grain; when he plotted rebellion, Emperor Taizong begged his life before the assembled ministers and could not obtain it, and in the end wept as he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke and his allies installed Yao Tingyun of the Right Guard as censor-in-chief and set him to impeach Wei Yuanzhong: "Hou Junji was a pillar of the founding order. When he rebelled, even Taizong pleaded before the court for his life—and failed, and wept as the sword fell.

sentences.zh: 其後房遺愛、薛萬徹、齊王祐等為逆，雖復懿親，皆從國法。

translations.literal: Afterward Fang Yi'ai, Xue Wanche, Prince You of Qi, and others committed treason; though they were again imperial kin of close degree, all were judged by the law of the state.
translations.idiomatic: After them came Fang Yi'ai, Xue Wanche, Prince You of Qi—royal blood every one, yet the law took them all the same.

sentences.zh: 元忠功不逮君集，身又非國戚，與李多祚等謀反，男入逆徒，是宜赤族污宮。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong's merit does not reach Junji's, and his person is moreover not imperial kin; he plotted rebellion with Li Duozuo and others, and his son entered the ranks of the rebels—he ought to suffer extermination of his clan and defilement of the palace women of his household.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong's service falls short of Junji's, and he is no imperial relative. He conspired with Li Duozuo; his son marched with the rebels. By every precedent his clan should be extinguished and his household women enslaved.

sentences.zh: 但有朋黨飾辭營救，以惑聖聽，陛下仁恩，欲掩其過。

translations.literal: But there are factions that adorn their words to rescue him, thereby confusing the sage ear; Your Majesty's benevolent grace wishes to cover his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his faction dresses up excuses to cloud Your Majesty's judgment, and Your benevolence inclines toward mercy.

sentences.zh: 臣所以犯龍鱗、忤聖意者，正以事關宗社耳。」

translations.literal: The reason your servant dares touch the dragon's scales and go against the sage intent is precisely that the matter concerns the altars of the ancestral temple and soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: I risk Your wrath and speak against Your inclination only because the fate of the dynasty hangs on this."

sentences.zh: 上頗然之。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor was considerably persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong was largely convinced.

sentences.zh: 元忠坐系大理，貶渠州司馬。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review and demoted to military adjutant of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was jailed in the Court of Judicial Review and demoted to military adjutant in Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客令給事中冉祖雍奏言：「元忠既犯大逆，不應出佐渠州。」

translations.literal: Zong Chuke had Attendant Ran Zuyong memorialize, saying: "Yuanzhong has already committed great treason and ought not to be sent out to serve as adjutant in Qu Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke had Attendant Ran Zuyong argue: "Yuanzhong committed treason—he must not be sent to serve even as adjutant in Qu Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 楊再思、李嶠亦贊之。

translations.literal: End of speech. Yang Zaisi and Li Jiao also endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Yang Zaisi and Li Jiao seconded the motion.

sentences.zh: 上謂再思等曰：「元忠驅使日久，朕特矜容，制命已行，豈宜數改！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zaisi and the others: "Yuanzhong has served at my command for many days; I have specially shown him forbearance. The edict has already been issued—how can it be changed repeatedly!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong told Zaisi and the rest: "Yuanzhong served me long and faithfully. I showed him mercy; the decree is already promulgated. It cannot be rewritten again and again!

sentences.zh: 輕重之權，應自朕出。

translations.literal: The authority to decide severity and leniency ought to come from me alone.
translations.idiomatic: The power to weigh punishment and pardon belongs to me alone.

sentences.zh: 卿等頻奏，殊非朕意！」

translations.literal: Your repeated memorials are utterly contrary to my intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Your repeated petitions run against my will!"

sentences.zh: 再思等惶懼拜謝。

translations.literal: End of speech. Zaisi and the others, fearful and alarmed, bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zaisi and the others fell to their knees in terror and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 監察御史袁守一復表彈元忠曰：「重俊乃陛下之子，猶如昭憲；

translations.literal: Censor Yuan Shouyi again submitted a memorial impeaching Yuanzhong, saying: "Chongjun was Your Majesty's own son, yet the law was made manifest;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuan Shouyi impeached Yuanzhong again: "Chongjun was Your Majesty's son, and the law was enforced without mercy;

sentences.zh: 元忠非勳非戚，焉得獨漏嚴刑！」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong is neither a meritorious minister nor imperial kin—how can he alone escape severe punishment!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong is no founding hero, no royal kin—why should he alone escape the harshest penalty!"

sentences.zh: 甲辰，又貶元忠務川尉。

translations.literal: End of speech. On the day jiachen, Yuanzhong was again demoted to magistrate of Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. On jiachen day Yuanzhong was demoted again—to magistrate of Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，楚客又令袁守一奏言：「則天昔在三陽宮不豫，狄仁傑奏請陛下監國，元忠密奏以為不可，此則元忠懷逆日久，請加嚴誅！」

translations.literal: Before long, Chuke again had Yuan Shouyi memorialize, saying: "In the past when Empress Zetian was unwell at Sanyang Palace, Di Renjie memorialized requesting that Your Majesty supervise the state; Yuanzhong secretly memorialized that this was not permissible—this shows Yuanzhong harbored treason for many days; please add severe execution!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chuke had Yuan Shouyi raise a new charge: "When Empress Wu fell ill at Sanyang Palace, Di Renjie urged Your Majesty to assume regency. Yuanzhong secretly argued against it—proof that his disloyalty is of long standing. Execute him without delay!"

sentences.zh: 上謂楊再思等曰：「以朕思之，人臣事主，必在一心；

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor said to Yang Zaisi and the others: "As I consider it, a minister serving his lord must be of one heart;
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong told Yang Zaisi and the others: "As I see it, a loyal minister serves his lord with a single heart;

sentences.zh: 豈有主上小疾，遽請太子知事！

translations.literal: how can there be, when the lord above has a minor illness, an immediate request that the crown prince administer affairs!
translations.idiomatic: would he at the first hint of illness demand that the crown prince take the reins?

sentences.zh: 此乃仁傑欲樹私恩，未見元忠有失。

translations.literal: This was Di Renjie wishing to plant private favor; I do not see that Yuanzhong was at fault.
translations.idiomatic: That was Di Renjie currying private favor. I see no fault in Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 守一欲借前事以陷元忠，其可乎！」

translations.literal: Shouyi wishes to borrow an old matter to entrap Yuanzhong—how can that be permitted!"
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi means to dredge up old history to destroy Yuanzhong—is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 楚客乃止。

translations.literal: End of speech. Chuke then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Chuke backed off.

sentences.zh: 元忠行至涪陵而卒。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong traveled as far as Fuling and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong died on the road at Fuling.

sentences.zh: 銀青光祿大夫、上庸公、聖善、中天、西明三寺主慧范於東都作聖善寺，長樂坡作大像，府庫為之虛耗。

translations.literal: Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Duke of Shangyong, and abbot of the three monasteries Shengshan, Zhongtian, and Ximing—Huifan—built Shengshan Monastery in the eastern capital and a great image at Changle Slope; the treasury was emptied by it.
translations.idiomatic: Huifan, Silver-Gleaming Grand Master, Duke of Shangyong, and abbot of Shengshan, Zhongtian, and Ximing monasteries, raised Shengshan Temple in the eastern capital and a colossal statue at Changle Slope—the imperial coffers were drained dry.

sentences.zh: 上及韋後皆重之，勢傾內外，無敢指目者。

translations.literal: The emperor and Empress Wei both held him in high esteem; his power tilted inside and outside, and none dared point or gaze at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and Empress Wei both favored him; his influence eclipsed court and capital alike, and no one dared even look his way.

sentences.zh: 戊申，侍御史魏傳弓發其奸贓四十餘萬，請置極法。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Remonstrating Censor Wei Chuanggong exposed his corrupt gains of more than four hundred thousand, and requested the utmost penalty.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Remonstrating Censor Wei Chuanggong uncovered more than four hundred thousand in embezzled funds and demanded the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 上欲宥之，傳弓曰：「刑賞國之大事，陛下賞已妄加，豈宜刑所不及！」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to pardon him; Chuanggong said: "Punishment and reward are great affairs of the state. Your Majesty has already bestowed rewards recklessly—how can punishment fail to reach where it should!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong meant to spare him. Chuanggong replied: "Reward and punishment are the pillars of state. Your Majesty has already lavished favor without cause—will you now withhold justice?"

sentences.zh: 上乃削黜慧范，放於家。

translations.literal: End of speech. The emperor then stripped and dismissed Huifan, releasing him to his home.
translations.idiomatic: End of speech. Zhongzong stripped Huifan of rank and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 宦官左監門大將軍薛思簡等有龐於安樂公主，縱暴不法，傳弓奏請誅之，御史大夫竇從一懼，固止之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Left Gate General Xue Sijian and others had the favor of Princess Anle and indulged in violence and lawlessness; Chuanggong memorialized requesting their execution, but Censor-in-Chief Dou Congyi grew afraid and firmly stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xue Sijian, Left Gate General, and others basked in Princess Anle's patronage and ran riot beyond the law. Wei Chuanggong petitioned for their execution, but Censor-in-Chief Dou Congyi, terrified, blocked the move.

sentences.zh: 時宦官用事，從一為雍州刺史及御史大夫，誤見訟者無須，必曲加承接。

translations.literal: At this time eunuchs wielded power; Cong Yi served as Prefect of Yongzhou and as Censor-in-Chief, and whenever he mistakenly saw a litigant without a beard, he would invariably bend the rules to show him favor.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs now held sway at court. Cong Yi was prefect of Yongzhou and Censor-in-Chief; whenever he happened to see a beardless litigant, he would invariably bend the rules to favor him.

sentences.zh: 以楊再思為中書令，韋巨源、紀處訥並為侍中。

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi was made Palace Attendant, and Wei Juyuan and Ji Chunna were both made Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi was appointed Palace Attendant, and Wei Juyuan and Ji Chunna were both made Directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，改左、右羽林千騎為萬騎。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, the Left and Right Forest of Plumes Thousand Riders were renamed Ten Thousand Riders.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the Left and Right Forest of Plumes regiments were expanded from Thousand Riders to Ten Thousand Riders.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑，命左屯衛將軍張仁願充朔方道大總管，以擊突厥。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day dingchou, Left Defender General Zhang Renyuan was appointed Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit to attack the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingchou, Left Defender General Zhang Renyuan was appointed Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit to strike the Turks.

sentences.zh: 比至，虜已退，追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the barbarians had already withdrawn; he pursued and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the enemy had already withdrawn; he pursued them and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 習藝館內教蘇安恆，矜高好奇，太子重俊之誅武三思也，安恆自言「此我之謀」。

translations.literal: Su Anheng, inner instructor at the Hall for Practicing the Arts, was proud and fond of the unusual; when Crown Prince Chongjun killed Wu Sansi, Anheng declared of himself, "This was my plan."
translations.idiomatic: Su Anheng, an inner instructor at the Hall for Practicing the Arts, was proud and eccentric. When Crown Prince Chongjun killed Wu Sansi, Anheng boasted, "That was my scheme."

sentences.zh: 太子敗，或告之；

translations.literal: When the crown prince was defeated, someone reported him;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's coup failed, someone informed on him;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，伏誅。

translations.literal: on the day wuyin, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: on wuyin he was executed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day yichou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of yichou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上遣使者分道詣江、淮贖生。

translations.literal: That year, the emperor sent envoys by separate routes to the Yangtze and Huai to ransom living creatures.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor sent envoys by separate routes to the Yangtze and Huai regions to buy back living creatures destined for slaughter.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人房子李又上疏諫曰：「江南鄉人采捕為業，魚鱉之利，黎元所資。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Li You of Fangzi submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying, "In the south of the Yangtze, country folk make their living by gathering and catching; the profit of fish and turtles is what the black-haired people rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafting Officer Li You of Fangzi submitted a memorial arguing, "In the lands south of the Yangtze, villagers live by fishing and gathering; fish and turtles are the common people's livelihood.

sentences.zh: 雖雲雨之私有沾於末類；

translations.literal: Though it is said that Heaven's rain and clouds privately moisten even the lowest creatures;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mercy may extend even to the smallest creatures;

sentences.zh: 而生成之惠未洽於平人。

translations.literal: the grace of nurturing life has not yet reached ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: yet the blessing of nurturing life has not reached ordinary folk.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 江湖之饒，生育無限，府庫之用，支供易殫。

translations.literal: The abundance of rivers and lakes breeds without limit, while the uses of the treasury are easily exhausted in supporting expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and lakes teem without limit, but the treasury's resources are easily exhausted.

sentences.zh: 費之若少，則所濟何成！

translations.literal: If the expense is slight, what good can be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Spend too little and the relief accomplishes nothing!

sentences.zh: 用之倘多，則常支有闕。

translations.literal: If the expenditure is great, ordinary outlays will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Spend too much and routine expenditures will fall short.

sentences.zh: 在於拯物，豈若憂人！

translations.literal: To save creatures—is that better than caring for people!
translations.idiomatic: To rescue creatures—is that wiser than caring for people!

sentences.zh: ，且鬻生之徒，唯利斯視，錢刀日至，網罟年滋，施之一朝，營之百倍。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who sell living creatures look only to profit; coin comes day by day, nets and traps increase year by year—give once and they will scheme a hundredfold return.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who trade in living creatures care only for profit. Money flows in daily; nets and traps multiply yearly. One day's bounty from the court becomes a hundredfold business for them.

sentences.zh: 未若回救贖之錢物，減貧無之徭賦，活國愛人，其福勝彼。」

translations.literal: Better to turn back the money and goods used for ransom, reduce corvée and taxes on the poor and destitute, revive the state and cherish the people—the blessing would surpass that.
translations.idiomatic: Better to redirect the ransom funds, lighten corvée and taxes on the destitute, and revive the state by cherishing the people—that would bring a greater blessing.
